name: Crush
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I walk well on a harness and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have bilateral nuclear sclerosis. Please read below for more information!

Crush is a sweet gentleman who has come to us from a breeder and is still waiting for his forever home. After spending all his life breeding, he is now finally getting to experience the love and kindness he deserves, and his confidence has truly blossomed during his time with us. He has learned to walk on a lead and is doing so well, showing us just how much he has to offer!

Crush is a lovely, chilled and laid-back boy who gets on wonderfully with other dogs. He gets super excited when meeting new friends out on walks and can turn into a playful pup, which is so lovely to see! He also enjoys a good run around in the yards with his kennel friends before settling down again. Crush can happily live with other resident dogs, and in the right home, we feel he could possibly be an only dog too.

Crush has also been a little star for his bath and groom, happily allowing himself to be scrubbed, blow-dried and even having a little face trim. He really is a fluffy white ball of perfection! He will make a lovely companion for someone looking for a gentle, easygoing boy to share their home with.

Crush has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient as he learns about house training and adjusts to a new routine. He could live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that he may need some time to settle into his new surroundings. With his lovely progress so far, we hope he will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy all the little things that make home life so special.

Crush has bilateral nuclear sclerosis, which will need to be monitored in his new home, although it does not appear to bother him at present. He also has the potential for chronic skin issues and dental disease that will need to be monitored, and he has already had two teeth extracted while with us.

Crush has spent so many years waiting for his chance to be loved, and now we desperately hope someone will see what a wonderful boy he is. He has so much love to give and deserves to spend his golden years enjoying the comforts of a forever home, with a cosy bed, kind people and all the love he has missed out on for so long.

Crush has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

How is this sweet gentleman still waiting for his home? At 9 years old, Crush wants nothing more than a place to call home. He’s spent all his years breeding until finally arriving with us where he has been showered with love, met new friends and even to walk lead! His confidence truly has bloomed in the last few months.

He is perfect around other dogs and gets super excited when meeting others out on walks and turns into a playful pup. He’s a very chilled and laid back boy but he does enjoy a good run around in the yards with his friends.

Crush had a bath and groom with me a few days ago and he was perfect. He allowed me to scrub him down and also blow dry him before giving him a little face trim.

The boy truly is a fluffy white ball of perfection!

Crush can live with other resident dogs and in the right home could possibly be an only.

Crush is a fairly nervous boy who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. He can be very shy and tends to rely heavily on his kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so he will need time and patience as he settles into his new surroundings.

Crush will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in the home that he can look to and lean on as he learns about home life and begins to build his confidence. He has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be understanding as he learns all about house training and adjusts to a new routine.

Crush is walking well on a harness, so he would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with the resident dog when he is settled in.

He could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that he will need plenty of time and space to settle in and begin to trust. Crush is a lovely boy who simply needs plenty of TLC, patience, and kindness as he finds his paws in the world.

He has come to us with bilateral nuclear sclerosis that will need to be monitored in his new home, and does not seem to bother him at this time. The vet has noted that he has a potential for chronic skin issues and dental disease that will need to be monitored in his new home. He has had two teeth extracted with us.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Norway
description:
I can live with older dog-savvy children who understand I need time to settle in.

I am young enough to be an only be homed with other dogs or even live with cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I would love plenty of adventures once I am fully vaccinated!

I am just a puppy! Please be patient with me while I learn the basics!

I will need to be neutered when I am of age!

20-10-26 Norway is a cute little boy who has come to us from a breeder along with his sibling as an unsold puppy. He is a cheeky, playful and mischievous little boy who is full of puppy fun and everything you could want in a companion!

Norway is young enough to be an only dog in his new home, provided his adopters have plenty of time to spend with him and keep him entertained, or he could live with a kind resident dog who doesn't mind having a playful puppy around. He could also live with older, dog-savvy children who are sensible and understand that he is still growing and learning about the world, and will need help understanding boundaries.

As Norway is still a puppy, his adopters will need to teach him all the basics, including house training, walking on a lead and all the other important skills he will need to become a happy and well-rounded adult dog. His new family will need to commit to taking him to puppy socialisation and training classes to help him learn and grow into the best boy he can be. His adopters will also need to agree to have him castrated when he is old enough.

Norway is a lovely little boy who has so much to offer, and we are sure he will bring plenty of fun, laughter and love to his forever home. He is ready to start his new adventure and find a family who will help him grow into a wonderful companion.

Norway has been given the Gift of Life byFelicity Mathie

name: Chewwie
description:
I’d like a quiet home filled with love and kindness!

I would like a home with a female dog medium size or larger. I am fine with cats.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 2 teeth removed!

Chewwie originally came to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He was lucky enough to be adopted, but sadly, despite being very loved, it became clear that the home wasn't quite the right match for him and he has now returned to our care to begin his search once again. Chewwie was very worried of the adult sons in the home and also wasn't a great match with the smaller resident dog.

Chewwie is a sensitive boy who had experienced very little before coming into rescue and can find unfamiliar situations overwhelming. In his previous home, he formed a very close bond with his female adopter and absolutely adored her, but remained worried around the adult sons in the household. For this reason, he is looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him all the time he needs to settle and build trust.

Since returning to our care, however, Chewwie has been an absolute pleasure. From the day he came back, he has been nothing but gentle, loving and affectionate with everyone here. Despite being returned because he was said to be nervous, we have seen a completely different side to him in kennels. He happily bounces over to greet us, is always looking for a fuss, and simply loves being around people. His affectionate nature shines through every day, and he has reminded us just what a special boy he is.

Although he had never lived in a home before his adoption, Chewwie adapted beautifully to family life. He was house trained and thoroughly enjoyed all the comforts of home, especially curling up in his cosy beds. He did find being left alone quite worrying, so his new adopters will need to be around for most of the time initially and gradually build up any time spent alone as his confidence grows.

Chewwie will need another kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help reassure him and show him the ropes, but this dog will need to be female and cocker spaniel sized or larger. He previously shared his home with a cat and happily ignored them, so he could potentially live with a dog-savvy cat.

Since being adopted, Chewwie has learnt to walk nicely on a lead and now really enjoys his walks, although he can still be worried in unfamiliar places and will benefit from ongoing encouragement as his confidence continues to grow.

Once Chewwie knows you, he is an incredibly loving and affectionate companion with a wonderfully cheeky personality. He loves playing with other dogs and is especially fond of his kennel friend. He's also a total water baby and absolutely loves splashing around in the paddling pool, making the most of every opportunity for fun. Like many mischievous youngsters, he has also been known to pinch things he shouldn't! His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially enjoys hard toys, while softer toys and enrichment items should be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.

Chewwie is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. His return to rescue has shown us just how affectionate, gentle and resilient he is, and we know that in the right home he will continue to flourish. In return, his lucky adopters will gain a devoted, fun-loving and wonderfully cheeky companion who will fill their days with smiles.

When Chewwie first arrived, he had a lick granuloma on his front leg, which healed well. Following his return to the rescue, he began limping on the same leg and holding it up. X-rays at a local veterinary practice showed no abnormalities or injuries, so it is thought to be a soft tissue injury which should continue to improve. His adopters and their own vet should continue to monitor this as a precaution. He has had 8 teeth removed.

Chewwie has been given the Gift of Life by Paula Elliot

Chewwie is probably the cheekiest boy on my section, and oh, how I love working with him every day. If he’s not booping his nose on my bum, he’s stealing my work folder, the treats, or anything else he can find!

He’s a big, loveable cloud, and once he trusts you, that bond is built forever. He can still be nervous of new people, but if you have treats, then he’s more than happy to take them from you, which is a huge step forward!

Anyone who takes Chewwie home is going to have a life full of laughter because this boy will definitely keep you occupied!

Chewwie is an absolute angel. From the day he arrived on my section, he's been nothing but gentle, loving, affectionate, and just a truly special soul.

Despite being returned because he was said to be nervous, I honestly haven't seen that side of him. With me, he's all about cuddles and attention. He'll happily bounce over to say hello and is always looking for affection. He's also got a cheeky side that keeps me smiling. If you leave your folder, phone, or radio lying around for even a second, don't be surprised if Chewwie decides it's his now!

He's a total water baby and absolutely loves splashing around in the pool with his kennel friend. Watching him let loose, have fun, and just be a dog is one of my favourite things. He also loves heading down to the big yard where he can have a good sniff, stretch his legs, and enjoy himself.

Chewwie really is such an amazing dog, and I feel so lucky to know him. Looking after him has been an absolute privilege.

Chewwie is a sensitive and nervous boy who had experienced very little before coming into rescue and still finds new situations quite overwhelming. In his previous home, he formed a very close bond with his female adopter and absolutely adored her, but he remained worried around men and struggled to relax around the adult sons in the household. He will therefore be looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him all the time he needs to settle and build trust.

Although he had never lived in a home before his adoption, Chewwie adapted beautifully to home life. He was house trained and thoroughly enjoyed all the comforts that a home has to offer, especially his cosy beds! He did find being left alone quite worrying, so his new adopters will need to be around for most of the time initially and slowly build up the amount of time he is left as his confidence grows.

Chewwie will need another kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help reassure him and show him the ropes, but this dog will need to be medium size or larger. He previously shared his home with a cat and happily ignored them, so he could potentially live with a dog savvy cat.

Since being adopted, Chewwie has also learnt how to walk on a lead and now enjoys his walks, although he can still be worried in unfamiliar places and will need ongoing support and encouragement as he continues to gain confidence.

Once Chewwie gets to know you, he is an incredibly loving and affectionate boy who adores a fuss and cuddle. He has a wonderfully cheeky personality and loves to play with other dogs. He is also a bit of a mischievous boy and has been known to pinch things he shouldn't! His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as we are told he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially loves hard toys, but softer toys and enrichment items will need to be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.

Chewwie is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. In the right home he will start to come out of his shell and truly flourish. In return, his lucky adopters will gain a devoted, affectionate and wonderfully cheeky friend who will make them smile every day.

When Chewwie first arrived he had a lick granuloma on his front leg, which healed well. When he returned to the rescue he was limping on his front leg and holding it up, we took him to a local vets for an x-ray and no abnormalities or injuries were found, so it's possible that it is a soft tissue injury which should start to feel better soon, but this is something his adopters and their vet will need to monitor.

description:

description:

name: Enfys
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

22-10-26 Enfys is the most wonderful girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. Shortly after Enfys arrived with us, we discovered she was pregnant and she soon gave birth to one puppy. She has been the most wonderful mum to little Eddie and now that he is old enough to find his forever home, Enfys is ready to start looking for her family too.

When she first arrived she was quite a worried girl, but she has settled in well and has really started to come out of her shell. She now absolutely adores the staff members who she knows well, but is still quite worried when meeting new people or experiencing new places, which is understandable.

Enfys is such a funny character, her favourite thing in the world is to roll over onto her back, which has been affectionately called her "diva downs" by those who know her! She loves to do zoomies around the play yard in the mornings while she waits for her breakfast to be prepared! We think with time, love and care she is going to blossom into the most wonderful girl.

Enfys can be quite worried, but can be an only dog in her home, with adopters who are able to offer her plenty of attention and time. However, she can live with another chilled dog who doesn't mind that she can be protective of her toys and will allow her to create her own safe space. She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will help her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+.

Enfys has never lived in a home before so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles in and learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She has learned all about walking on a lead and harness while being with us and walks well although can be unsure in new surroundings, so will need more practice to gain confidence.

Enfys is a lovely girl who is already showing us little flashes of her personality. She has so much potential, and we know that with the right experienced home, she will continue to blossom.

Our vet has noted that she has a Grade 1 patella luxation in her right hind leg, which will need to be monitored although may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. She has been treated for a skin rash and has some areas of alopecia.

name: Otis
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I have started harness training, but this is still new to me!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Otis has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He is an extremely nervous boy who is still finding the world a very scary place and is utterly petrified of human touch. When he first arrived, he would do everything he could to avoid being touched, frantically running around the yard to escape contact. Although he was interested in people, he simply didn't feel brave enough to let them close.

Otis is now making small but lovely steps forward, although he is still extremely worried about touch, with those who he knows very well he will tentatively accept chin tickles, though is still very worried about this. He still needs to build his confidence, and getting him comfortable with human hands will be a slow process that is likely to continue well into his new home. His adopters must be prepared to work at his pace, without rushing or putting pressure on him.

At just one year old, Otis has plenty of typical Labrador puppy character waiting to shine through. He loves tennis balls and soft toys and is still figuring out how to play fetch! As his confidence grows, we're beginning to see more of his funny, silly personality, and we hope there is lots more to come.

Otis absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort and reassurance from their company. He will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help him feel safe and guide him as he learns about life in a home. Having a canine friend by his side will be particularly important while he continues to build trust in people.

Otis will need a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the time and patience they need. He has never lived in a home before, so he will need help learning all about home life, including house training. He will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to keep him safe while he gains confidence.

Otis has started harness training with his kennel mummy, and this will need to continue in his home at a slow and comfortable pace. This will need to be introduced gradually, starting in a safe environment and allowing him to progress at his own pace.

Otis is a special little boy who is trying so hard to be brave. With patient, understanding adopters and a confident canine companion, we believe he has the potential to blossom into a fun, loving and rewarding companion. He will need a family willing to celebrate the smallest steps forward and give him the time he needs to discover that the world can be a wonderful place.

Otis has been given the Gift of Life by Nic Johhston

Otis is a few weeks into his stay at Many Tears and honestly, he’s breaking my heart. That being said, he is progressing slowly, in his own funny way.

Otis is utterly petrified of human touch and when he first arrive he would do literally anything to get away from me. I mean truly frantic to avoid being touched. He would bolt away in the yard and do laps to avoid any contact. He wouldn’t take treats from my hand despite being a massive foodie! Yet when I turned around he would show interest to me and would nibble my hand through the gates. He so wanted to be brave and just didn’t know how.

We are slowly getting there, it’s not much of a progression to most people but he will freeze with me now and tentatively accept chin tickles. Small baby steps, we are already seeing progress! Desensitising Otis to human hands is not going to be a quick fix and will likely continue into his home life. He does now take treats from my hand, even in the yard but after each treat he does a little lap of the yard to ramp himself up for the next one! He really is such a funny little guy.

At just 1 years old, he has so much of your typical Lab puppy in him, but he just doesn’t feel safe enough to fully let it out. He loves a tennis ball and is still coming to grips with how fetch works. He loves soft toys and ADORES the company of other dogs and seeks so much comfort and support from them.

Once Otis is more comfortable being handled, our next milestone will be getting him in a harness to begin the road to exploring the world on walks!

He is such a character & the more confident he becomes, the more we get to see his funny, silly side. I really do believe he will settle into the most fulfilling, fun dog you could hope for & will make his future adopters very happy!

Otis has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He is a very nervous boy who is feeling very overwhelmed by all the changes in his life and is finding his surroundings quite scary at the moment. He is very worried about being handled and it is clear that he has not had much socialisation before, so he is in need of lots of patience, kindness and TLC.

Otis will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand that he will need plenty of time to settle in and build his confidence at his own pace. He will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in his new home to be his friend and companion and help show him the ropes. Having a confident canine friend by his side will be very important as Otis begins to learn that the world is not such a scary place.

Otis will also need a secure garden with 6ft+ fencing to keep him safe while he gains confidence. He has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be kind and understanding as he learns all about home life and new skills such as house training.

Otis doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and this will need to be introduced very gradually by practicing first in the garden, allowing him to gain confidence before venturing further afield.

Otis is a very worried boy who needs someone special to give him the time and understanding he deserves. With a calm environment, a confident canine companion and lots of patience and love, we hope that little by little he will begin to feel safe and discover the happy boy hiding underneath all those worries.

name: Maggie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I can be an only dog or live with one dog my size or larger. I cannot live with cats!

I'd like a secure garden to play in that has 6ft fencing.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been spayed and have had 4 teeth extracted.

Maggie spent the first few years of her life at a breeders & originally came to us when she was 5 years old. She was adopted in January 2025 & spent 16 months in a home. She ended up back in our care & has since waited to find her forever. Maggie really is just the sweetest, most special girl. Whilst she is shy at first, she bonds incredibly closely with her people. She has a cheeky, playful side & loves to fling herself around with a tennis ball. She bounces & prances around the yard just keeping herself entertained. Maggie is our girl who helps the scared dogs be brave. Maggie shows them how it’s done & truly she has been the helping hand for so many dogs since she has been with us. She has seen kennel friends come & go, yet she still waits in kennels. Maggie is a happy dog even in kennels, especially when she is with any of her favourite people. She is so affectionate & truly a little shadow. You gain a best friend when you’re loved by Maggie. Our groomer has said multiple times that she is an absolute delight to groom. Maggie loves nothing more than to roll around in mud, sand, leaves, she gets mucky quickly. Her & our groomer are well acquainted now so she is well adjusted to grooming.

Sadly, Maggie was returned to us following an incident involving one of the smaller resident dogs in her previous home. While out in the garden one evening, Maggie became frightened by the other dog barking, and although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight. They struggled to make up or comfortably co-exist afterwards, so Maggie will need a carefully chosen home where everyone can feel safe and settled.

Maggie is looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and can give her plenty of time, patience and understanding to settle at her own pace. She can be worried by men and initially barked at the male resident in her previous home, although with time, patience and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. We are continuing to help her build positive relationships with men here, and she has bonded well with a male staff member who is part of her care team.

Maggie is very people-oriented and, once she knows and trusts you, she becomes an incredibly loving and devoted companion. She is particularly attached to her main carer and loves following her around, enjoying fuss and cuddles. When she first returned to us, she was very shy and unsure of new people, but she has since settled in wonderfully and has made lovely progress.

Although Maggie previously lived with another dog, her home will need careful consideration following her return. We would now consider her as an only dog in the right circumstances, with experienced adopters who have plenty of time to help her settle. Alternatively, she could live with a calm, confident resident dog of a similar size or larger. She has shared her kennel with several different dogs since returning and has been wonderful with them, happily sharing food and toys. She also enjoys play dates with a larger group of dogs in our big play yard. I cannot live with cats, so I will need a home without small furries.

Maggie is very food-motivated and loves her treats, which will be helpful when settling into her new home. She can already walk nicely on a lead and harness without pulling and will often check back with you for reassurance. Having previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with home life, although she may need some reminders of her house training.

On one occasion in her previous home, Maggie became tangled in her harness and panicked, biting the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. This was an isolated incident caused by fear, but it is important that her new family understands how she may react when frightened or overwhelmed. She will need calm, gentle handling and people who can recognise when she is worried and give her the reassurance and space she needs.

Maggie has also shown that when she feels stressed or overwhelmed, she may try to escape by climbing. For this reason, she will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft to help keep her safe.

Maggie has had four teeth extracted, and this should be kept in mind as part of her veterinary history.

Maggie has so much love to give to the people she trusts. In the right calm and understanding home, with experienced, patient and dog-savvy adopters who allow her to settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to flourish and become a truly wonderful companion.

Maggie has yet again made some new canine friends here at the rescue, Jinx - Hound and Hayley - Poodle and yet again she has been amazing with them, showing them that us staff here at the rescue are nothing to be feared and helping them understand that a human touch can be loving and kind, she has been incredible with a lot of our scardies and the change you then see in those dogs, a lot of it thanks to Maggie, is amazing, she really is a special girl.I also had to bath her (again) this past week as due to her fur type and the weather she gets dirty rather easily, but, she is so good in the bath, she's very tolerant of the water and being shampooed. When it comes to brushing and drying, she is also easy, for the most part she either just stands or lays there which makes her quicker to dry.She really is a dream dog and she's still waiting for her forever home after almost 5 months. Winter is coming, that means cold days and nights, and although we do everything we can here at the rescue to ensure that they're all comfy and warm, it's nothing compared to the home comforts of being wrapped up in her own blanket, snuggled up with her own family knowing, who wouldn't want that for her?Please consider Maggie, she's one of our most overlooked angels and it genuinely makes me sad that no one seems to take an interest in her. I promise you she'll make an amazing companion and a true best friend just like she is for me while I'm her kennel mum.

Maggie aka Magaluf, Magarita, Mags or Miss Maggie is a special girl. She's the kind of dog that once she's comfortable with you, you instantly feel the love she has for you from her and it's such a lovely feeling, she is very affectionate and loves her people more than anything, well, maybe not more than her food or treats but we're her second favourite.

Maggie's confidence has grown so much these past months that she's even helped some of our more shyer residents come out of their shells, and by them seeing how she is with us makes them realise that they too can be like that with us and have fusses and cuddles etc.

She is an incredible girl and it truly baffles me as to why she keeps getting overlooked. She is beautiful both inside and out and has such a fun personality. She is good with other dogs but won't necessarily need to be rehomed with another dog as we believe that she is confident enough to be an only.

Maggie will become a best friend and a true companion, and I know I'm probably a lot biased being one of her kennel mums but she truly is so so special and anyone would be lucky to have her in their life.

Maggie has settled into rescue life beautifully, but having spent over a year in a home, we are really desperate to get her back into one ASAP!

Since her arrival, Maggie has been kenneled with our lovely Bocker Eddie whom she gets along with wonderfully. She does enjoy her time with him, and would happily live alongside one resident dog - male or female, her size or larger!!

During Maggie’s time here she has formed a wonderful bond with her kennel mums who she absolutely dotes on. She’s even bonded with a kennel dad who has said she’s an absolute sweetheart, and he’s had no trouble with her too, which is so good to hear.

Maggie's kennel mummies describe her as loyal, affectionate, and loving. She really looks to them for reassurance, and when they’re around nothing else matters. Seeing as she’s grown so much in confidence, we’re happy to say she can now also be homed as an only dog too in the circumstance her adopters have lots of time to spend with her!!

Maggie isn’t really too fussed on playing with toys, but what she does love is her food & treats so gaining her trust will be a breeze!

A dog like Maggie is absolutely wasted in kennels, she’s already lived a life at home & we are so desperate to get her back into one!!

Maggie is a sweet Cockapoo who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

Maggie is a very shy and sensitive girl who is wary of strangers, although she does allow handling. She is trying very hard to be brave and is beginning to show small signs of progress, even getting close to taking treats from our hands, though she is not quite confident enough just yet.

Maggie is not yet confident enough to be an only dog, so we feel she would settle best in a home with one calm and confident resident dog of a similar size or larger, who can help her feel safe and reassured as she adjusts.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with the sights and sounds of a home environment. However, she may still need some support with house training as she settles into a new routine. Maggie can already walk on a lead, so she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with the resident dog when she is settled in.

Maggie is particularly worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home. With time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. Unfortunately, there was also an incident where Maggie became tangled in her harness and, in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. Because of this, Maggie will need a calm adult-only home with patient and understanding adopters who have experience or understanding of the challenges that can come with rehoming ex-breeding dogs.

Since Maggie has been with us, she has shown that when she feels stressed or overwhelmed, she may try to find a way to escape by climbing. Because of this, she will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft to help keep her safe and prevent any potential escape attempts.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and slowly come out of her shell.

Maggie is currently being treated for an ear infection in the left ear.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Sixpence
description:
I will need an adult only home, that will let me settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I can be a little nervous, and will need a secure garden to learn about the outdoors.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Sixpence is a nervous girl who has come to us from a breeder. She isn’t brave enough to approach you just yet, but she is easy to handle once she is in your arms. We have now learnt that she is trying so hard to be brave and, although she is still quite nervous, we are seeing little bits of her cheeky Daxi personality coming through every day.

Sixpence seems to have had very little positive touch or affection before coming to us. She has recently moved in to foster and is happy to take treats from her foster parents but is not quite sure about being stroked yet. She will allow them to put her harness on as long as she is in a quiet corner and things are taken slowly. You can tell she isn't entirely comfortable, but she trusts us enough to allow it and is always very happy to enjoy a little cheese reward afterwards! With continued positive reinforcement, we are confident that this will improve as Sixpence learns that good things can come from new experiences.

Sixpencerelies heavily on other dogs and really enjoys being around her resident dog friends. She watches what they do and follows their lead for confidence, and she has even learnt from them how to use the dog steps to get onto the sofa and watch the world go by from the front window! She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she continues to find her confidence and learn about home life.

Penny is also discovering all sorts of things that she enjoys. She loves sunbathing, having the freedom to explore a secure dog field, stuffed teddies and, of course, cheese! name: Moxy
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like an extra-secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I am currently in a foster home where I am learning about home life!

Moxy is a worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder and is now in foster, where she is beginning to show her lovely, affectionate personality. She is still a little nervous and can be unsure around new people, but as she learns that she can trust you, we are seeing more of her sweet side. In the evenings, Moxy will come up to her fosterers for a cuddle on her own terms, which is lovely to see as she continues to grow in confidence.

Moxy will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time, patience and kindness to settle into her new life. A calm, quiet home with minimal disruption will be important, allowing her to feel safe and build a bond with her new family at her own pace. She will also need a kind and confident resident dog to help her continue building her confidence and show her the ropes.

Moxy has never lived in a home before and is currently learning about house training and the routines of home life in her foster home. Her new family will need to continue helping her with these things patiently, as well as gently introducing her to walking on a lead. Moxy has shown signs of digging in her foster home, so she will need an extra-secure garden to help keep her safe while she explores outside.

Moxy arrived with sore eyes, and our vet noted that her lower eyelid is irregular, although it is not currently causing her any issues. Her vision is also slightly reduced, but she gets around well and this doesn't stop her from enjoying life. She also arrived with sore skin and old concrete sores, which we hope will continue to improve.

Moxy has already come such a long way, and it is wonderful to see her slowly learning to trust the people around her. She may not be the kind of girl who immediately runs up to greet you, but with time, patience and a calm home where she can feel safe, we know she has so much more to give. We would love to find Moxy the special family who will let her settle at her own pace and discover just how lovely life can be.

Moxy has been on our section for a few weeks now & she is such a delight to be around.

Dependent on where Moxy is will decide which side of Moxy you will get. Both sides are a truly beautiful dog, but one is incredibly sad & shut down and the other is a wonderful, affectionate girl who truly tries her hardest to be brave.

When in the kennel you’ll find Moxy in the back, she’ll appear sad, broken & totally overwhelmed. She tries to dig a lot, and burrow herself behind any beds she can find. We have swapped these beds out with a big comfy duvet now where she likes to chill in the corner. However I do think she sees it as her safe space, where she will hide from the outside world. Once she’s out of that kennel, and running to the yard she will wag her body in its entirety as she greets other kennels desperately trying to make new friends.

Even in the yard, Moxy can still feel overwhelmed and will sit in the corner & dig at times, and we’ve even tried taking her out on a harness but she remains frozen. But once she’s comfortable in the company she is around, she is the most affectionate girl. She happily sits next to you, gives you kisses and that tail really does not stop wagging. Her company is joyous, and being one of her trusted people is so incredibly rewarding, and brightens every day I spend with her.

Moxy’s people will need to take it easy with her, need to understand exbreeders, and be patient & kind along her journey at home. Mixing her nervous character along with her poor eyesight, being at home is likely to be very scary for her. As one of her kennel mummies, I can vouch for her & tell you that gaining her trust, and gaining her as a family member will be the most fulfilling experience, and one I am extremely jealous of. Moxy deserves love, care & a place to feel safe after all this time feeling scared & overwhelmed.

Moxy, like a lot of ex breeder dogs, is a very nervous dog. When I first met her, she wouldn’t leave the back, didn’t want me to get near her and I had to carry her back and forth from the yard. On my second day with Moxy, she ran straight to the yard as I opened her kennel door and, once I entered the yard, she was jumping all over me, kissing me, genuinely thrilled to see me. This is behaviour that truly shocked me in the best possible way.

It’s now been a couple of weeks since I first worked with her and the affection she shows me and the confidence she found has only grown. She’s truly incredible.Around new people, she reverts back to shutting down and hiding in the back. Despite this, we still have an incredible relationship. Moxy needs to be shown she can trust you.

Once this girl trusts you, you’ll see the same side I see. You won’t see this side if you met her on a show around of our kennels or even if you were let in her kennel to socialise her. This is something you can only experience from adopting her and progressing her like we do. I truly love her with all my heart. Take a chance on her and I have no doubts you’ll experience the same as I.

Moxy is a very worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is feeling quite overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment and is in need of lots of TLC, patience and reassurance. Once she gets to know you, she does start to come out of her shell and then enjoys a gentle fuss.

Moxy will need a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need plenty of time to settle in at her own pace. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her learn how wonderful her life can be now. We would consider homing her with old, dog savvy teenagers.

Moxy has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. Her new family will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life, including new skills like house training and walking on a lead. She will need gentle encouragement and understanding as she settles in.

Moxy is a very sweet girl who has had a difficult start in life. She now needs someone who will give her the time, patience and love she needs to blossom. With a kind canine friend by her side and a quiet, understanding home, we hope she will slowly gain confidence and discover how lovely life can be.

Moxy has arrived with slightly sore eyes and our vet has noted her low eyelid is irregular but doesn't feel this is causing her any issues at the moment, but will need to be monitored moving forwards. Although she can see, her vision isn't the best, but she doesn't let this slow her down and gets around well. She also arrived with sore skin and old concrete sores, which will hopefully feel much better soon.

name: Louise
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home with experienced adopters.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am not ready to learn about lead walking yet. A garden is fine for now.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and can still find people and handling very frightening. However, she has made lovely progress since arriving and is showing us more of her cheeky personality every day.

Over the past month, Louise has grown in confidence. While she is still very worried about being touched and picked up, she is no longer as shut down as she was when she first arrived. She is now more than happy to come over for treats and will sit close by while waiting for more. She likes to use her voice to let everyone know how she is feeling, is very partial to chasing flies, and has quite a big personality packed into such a tiny dog. It is wonderful to see her becoming more comfortable in her surroundings.

Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her as she settles into family life.

Louise can be vocal around food and may give a warning growl, but she does not actually do anything and this appears to simply be her way of communicating that she would like some space. She can happily be fed alongside her canine friends as long as each dog has their own bowl and they stick to their own food. She is also absolutely fine taking treats, so this is something her adopters should continue to manage calmly and sensibly.

Louise is slowly becoming more comfortable with being handled, and gentle work has begun to help her get used to being picked up. This is still very worrying for her and she can become wriggly and panic when lifted, but she has never tried to bite during these sessions. With time and patience, we hope she will continue to learn that she is safe and that nobody is going to hurt her.

Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns the basics, including house training. She is not yet ready for harness training, so her future family will need to carefully plan how and when to introduce this once she feels more secure. Everything must happen at Louise's pace so that she can continue building confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Louise is a sensitive little soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her flourish. Every small step she takes is a huge achievement, and she continues to surprise us with just how much she is growing in confidence. With experienced adopters, kind canine companions and lots of love, we truly believe Louise will continue to blossom into the wonderful little dog we know she can become.

Louise has been given the Gift of Life by Ann Winter

Louise has been with us for about 3 months now and even though she has progressed since she first arrived, things are happening very slowly and steadily. I would have liked for her to have gained more confidence by this point, but some dogs struggle with being in such a busy kennel environment to let their guard down … and Louise is one of them! That’s okay though. Making sure she’s happy and content within herself is the most important thing, and I’d say she is!

I haven’t really pushed Louise too far out of her comfort zone up until now, just because I didn’t want to send her backwards with her progress, but there does come a point where you have to, to prove to them that it’s okay. So today I took Louise into my grooming room for a very gentle and calm brushing session. She didn’t want to stand on the grooming table and kept clambering back onto me - which is the first time she’s ever done that - so I opted to keep her on my lap while I brushed her. She was settled for the most part, but she did have a little panic when we got to her ears as she had a couple of tangles which must have hurt her. I managed to cut them out with a scissors and then she was okay with me brushing around that area. I kept the session very short and sweet as I didn’t want to push too far, and I think it was the right decision. When I took her back to the kennel she didn’t sprint away from me or anything like that, so I’d say our relationship is still there!

Louise is such a special little character, and I really hope someone will see her in the same way I do soon. She deserves a life outside of kennels, one where she can finally start to thrive.

Louise has been on my section with me for about a month now, and I’ve definitely seen some positive changes in her. She’s still terrified of being touched and picked up, but her overall confidence is improving daily. She’s now more than happy to come and take treats from me and sit close to me while she’s waiting for more. She’s also nowhere near as shut down as she was when she first arrived and is now turning into quite a cheeky monkey. She does like to use her voice to express her feelings, and she’s also very partial to chasing flies! She’s actually got quite a big personality for such a little girl, and it’s a pleasure to see it emerging as the days go by.I’ve been working slowly on getting Louise used to being picked up, and while she’s definitely still very worried about it, she has calmed down slightly. She’s never tried to bite me, but she does sometimes have little panics and becomes very wriggly when she’s in my arms. I do think this is something that will improve over time. She just needs some more practice and to realise that we’re not hurting her. She obviously hasn’t been handled a lot in her life, so now it’s up to us to prove to her that it’s okay.I love working with Louise, and I can really see the potential in her. She just needs someone to give her a chance and work with her through all her worries and fears. She’s not ready for harness training or conquering the outside world yet, so that’s something her future adopters will need to take into consideration and make a plan for. I do believe she’ll progress faster in a kind home with adopters who have lots of time and patience to give her, so I really hope she won’t have to wait here for much longer.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and currently finds people and handling very frightening. At the moment, Louise feels safest keeping her distance and, if pushed beyond her comfort zone, may make the wrong decision and nip purely out of fear. She is a very scared girl who needs understanding, patience and time.Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience of helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing.Although Louise takes great comfort from other dogs, she can show signs of resource guarding around food. For this reason, she will need to be fed separately from other dogs, and care will need to be taken when giving treats or other high-value food items. Her adopters will need experience of managing this behaviour and the confidence to do so appropriately.Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns new skills such as house training. She is not yet ready to begin learning about lead walking or wearing a harness, as handling is still very worrying for her. These things will need to be introduced gradually and at her pace once she feels more comfortable and secure.Louise is a sensitive soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her build confidence. We will continue to work with her every day, helping her take small steps forward at a pace she is comfortable with. In the right home, with the support of canine friends and experienced adopters, we hope Louise will slowly learn that people can be kind and that life has so much to offer.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe. I've never met cats so I'm unsure!

I am too scared to go out for walks right now and will need careful introduction.

I'm still learning house training, lead walking, and other basics of home life.

I’m fully vaccinated and spayed, ready for my forever home!

30-09-26 Hatty originally came to us from a breeder, and was adopted for a period of time, and was sadly returned to our care due to her adopter becoming unwell. She managed a recent vet visit incredibly well considering how worried she can be, allowing the vet to examine her and administer her vaccinations while she was safely cuddled in her blanket. We know that the right home for Hatty is out there, and that with someone who truly understands her, she can form an incredibly special bond.Hatty is a very worried little lady who has come such a long way since arriving with us. She finds human interaction incredibly stressful and can still be very timid and defensive when she feels she is going to be handled. However, she has made some lovely progress in her foster home and is showing us that, with the right person and plenty of patience, she can learn to feel safe.

Hatty will still need a blanket to help her feel comfortable when she needs to be picked up, and she can become frightened enough to toilet herself when she is worried about being handled. Once she is safely settled, she will allow gentle strokes around her face, head and back, although she is not comfortable with her feet being touched. Her foster home has found that she is happiest when she is given plenty of space and allowed to approach things at her own pace.

Hatty absolutely loves other dogs and is particularly happy around other Dachshunds. She gets very excited to see her dog friends and enjoys being around them, so she will need a confident resident dog in her new home who can help her feel safe and show her the ropes. She enjoys having a cosy space of her own to retreat to, but also loves being able to relax on the sofa alongside the other dogs.

Hatty is very treat motivated and will happily come over for treats, which is a lovely way for her adopters to build a positive relationship with her. She is content plodding around, observing what is going on and enjoying the company of her canine friends. She can be destructive if left alone, so her adopters will need to be prepared for this and ensure she has plenty of safe things to occupy her.

Hatty will need a very special home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand just how frightening the world can feel for her. She will need a quiet, adult-only home with someone who is around most of the time and who can give her the time and space she needs without placing expectations on her. She will need gentle handling and continued support with things such as toilet training and lead training, although walks may not be something she becomes comfortable with.

Hatty is not going to be an easy dog to rehome, but she is a very special and frightened girl who deserves someone willing to see past her worries. With a confident canine companion, a quiet home and an adopter who can give her the time and patience she needs, we believe Hatty can continue to flourish and discover just how lovely life can be.

name: Yasmin
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have an umbilical hernia that will be addressed at the time of my spay.

22-10-26 Yasmin is a quiet little girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She seems a little overwhelmed by her new surroundings, but she has been accepting of handling and is not overly scared. Yasmin is a shy girl who will need time, patience and gentle encouragement to help her feel safe and begin to build her confidence. However, the longer she has been with us, she has built some confidence and will approach to take some treat paste from you.

Yasmin would do well with a kind and gentle resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws. Having a friendly canine companion by her side should help her feel more secure as she adjusts to life in a home. Her adopters will need to have experience with ex-breeders to better understand her needs. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens who are sensible.

As Yasmin has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be understanding and allow her to progress at her own pace.

Yasmin has arrived with a large abdominal hernia, which our vets will address at the time of her spay.

With a calm, loving home and a little patience, we hope Yasmin will gradually grow in confidence and discover the comforts of being a cherished family member.

name: Kismet
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and have had an umbilical hernia repaired.

Kismet is a lovely girl who came to us from a breeder and has now moved to a wonderful foster home, where she is experiencing life in a home for the very first time. She has a sweet, gentle nature and is a curious, active little girl who is slowly finding her feet and learning that the world isn't such a scary place.

Kismet is still a little unsure of people, but she is making a lovely start in foster. She enjoys following her fosterer around and is happy to accept a gentle fuss, although she isn't quite brave enough to ask for attention herself just yet. She is beginning to settle into her new routine and sleeps quietly overnight snuggled up in a crate with her foster buddy, greeting her fosterer each morning with a lovely waggy tail. These little moments show that she is trying her best, and with time, patience and kindness, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence.

Kismet takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need a kind, friendly resident dog of a similar size in her new home. She would love a canine companion who enjoys snuggling up and sharing their bed, as having other dogs around helps her feel safe and secure while she gets used to her new surroundings.

Kismet is doing well with her toilet training when given regular opportunities to go out into the garden. She has also started learning to wear a harness, but she will need more time to build her confidence before beginning to learnt to walk on a lead, which can initially be introduced gently in the garden when she feels ready.

Kismet arrived with us very underweight, so she is currently being fed three meals a day in a crate to ensure she gets all the food she needs without her canine friends helping themselves! It will be important for her to continue enjoying a nutritious diet in her new home to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. She also had a small umbilical hernia, which was repaired at the time of her spay.

As this is Kismet's first experience of living in a home, she will need patient adopters who understand that everything is new to her and who will give her the time and encouragement she needs to settle at her own pace. She will also need someone around for most of the day while she adjusts to her new routine, with any time left alone introduced gradually as she becomes more confident. Kismet can live with sensible, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who will understand her need for patience and reassurance.

Kismet is making a lovely start in foster and has so much potential to blossom into a happy, confident little companion. With a loving family, a reassuring canine friend and plenty of patience, we hope she will continue to discover just how wonderful life in a home can be and find the forever home she deserves.

Kismet has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

Kismet has made a good start in foster. She has a sweet gentle nature, is curious, active, shadows her fosterer and sleeps quietly at night with her foster buddy Kylie in a crate, and greets me in the morning with a lovely waggy tail.

Kismet is underweight and is fed 3 meals a day in a crate so that she doesn’t allow the rest of the pack to help her out. With regular visits to the garden she is doing well with toilet training.

Harness training has started but lead walking will wait until she is more confident and then start in the garden. Kismet will accept a gentle fuss but does not ask for attention yet.

Kismet needs a home with at least one similar size playmate who likes to cosy up and share their bed as she takes great comfort from their presence and owners where someone is around most of the time while she settles into a new routine. Time alone will have to be built up gradually.

Kismet is a lovely, happy girl who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a semi-brave little girl who wants to be our friend, but just can't quite get there yet. If we need to pick her up, Kismet will lie down and accept the handling, and she will offer little kisses on our hands while wagging her tail. These small signs show that she is trying her best, even though she is still a little unsure.

Kismet gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Kismet has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to give her plenty of time, patience and encouragement while she gets used to her new surroundings. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in.

Kismet has arrived very underweight, so she will need a nutritious diet to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. This will need to be continued in her new home. She also has a small umbilical hernia, which has been repaired at the time of her spay.

Kismet is a sweet little girl who is clearly trying hard to be brave, and we hope that with the support of a kind canine companion and a loving, patient family, she will slowly gain confidence and discover just how lovely life in a home can be.

name: Helga
description:
I can live with older children, aged 13+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I would like to be the only animal in my new home.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home! Read below for more!

25-09-26 Helga is a wonderful lady who originally came to us a while ago and was adopted into a loving home, where she spent several happy years. Sadly, she has now returned to our care as it wasn't the right long-term match for her needs, and she is looking for a new home that understands her and can give her the life she deserves.

Helga generally mixes well with other dogs, but she can be quite selective about who she likes and can be unpredictable around certain dogs. For this reason, she will need to be the only dog in her new home, and her adopters will need previous experience with reactive dogs and an understanding of how to manage her around other dogs when out and about. She cannot live with cats or small furries and will also need to be kept on lead around birds and livestock.

When it comes to people, Helga is a complete big baby! She doesn't quite understand her size (47kg!) and loves nothing more than getting as close to you as possible, and will use your legs as her very own leaning post while she soaks up all the fuss. She has quickly become a favourite with everyone she meets and is such a lovely girl to have around. Despite her size, she has a lovely, calm temperament with people and is incredibly affectionate once she knows you.

She is an outgoing lady that would love to go on plenty of quiet adventures where she can enjoy the outdoors in peace. However, she can also be a lazy lady, and would love a home where she can enjoy being a couch potato.

Helga can live with sensible, dog-savvy older teenagers aged 13+ who understand her needs and will treat her with kindness and respect. Due to her size and strength, she can be quite strong on the lead, so any children in the home should not be responsible for walking her, as she could potentially overpower them if she reacts or becomes excited while out.

Having already lived in a home for several years, Helga understands the basics of home life and is house trained. However, her adopters should be prepared to give her a little patience and some gentle reminders while she settles back into a new routine. Moving home can be a big change, and we want Helga to have the time she needs to feel comfortable and secure again.

Helga is an amazing lady who has so much love to give. She does have some specific needs, but for the right person who understands her and is experienced with reactive dogs, she could be a wonderful companion. She just needs someone willing to look past her quirks, understand what makes her tick and give her the chance to find the right forever home.

Helga has arrived overweight and is now on a diet to help her back to a healthy weight. Her back legs seem to be affected by this and she is now on joint supplements to help her joints as she continues to lose the weight.

Helga's previous adopters had her DNA tested and this came back as 46% Giant Schnauzer, 44% Caucasian Shepherd Dog, 3% Saint Bernard, 2% Black Russian Terrier & 2% German Shepherd Dog.

name: Hayley
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs, I have not met cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and will enjoy going on adventures with my new family!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had an entropion repaired in my right eye.

Hayley is the sweetest, gentlest little girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived she was a little timid, but she soon settled in and started learning just how wonderful fuss and attention is. She has such a lovely, gentle nature and we know that with time, patience and plenty of kindness, she will blossom.

Hayley has recently moved to a wonderful foster home where she is getting to experience home life for the first time and is settling in well. She is a wonderful girl who loves fuss and attention and has been such a wonderful girl.

Hayley enjoys the company of other dogs and can be homed with a kind resident dog who doesn't mind sharing their space. In the right circumstances we would also consider homing her as an only dog as long as her adopters were around most of the time. Hayley is looking for adopters with plenty of time to spend with her and previous experience of dogs, who understand that she will need time to settle in to her new home. We feel she would benefit from a quiet, loving home where she can build her confidence and discover how wonderful life can be. We would consider Hayley living with gentle, dog-savvy children aged 9+.

As she has never lived in a home before moving to foster, her new family will need to give her plenty of time and understanding as she continues to learn all about home life and new skill like house training. She can already walk well on a lead, and will enjoy going for walks with her new family.

Hayley is such a precious, gentle girl who has so much potential. She just needs someone who will give her the time, patience and love she deserves while she learns what it means to be part of a family.

She arrived with an entropion in her right eye, which has been repaired by our vets.

Hayley has been given the Gift of Life by Diane Westwick

Hayley really is a smashing dog. She is laid back and so easy to love. She really loves to be loved and enjoys being out in the secure field. She is in foster with 4 small dogs and is submissive of anything.

Hayley is a gentle, sweet, inoffensive soul who just wants to feel loved. She would rather a cuddle than treat and has been the perfect house guest.

Hayley is the sweetest, gentlest little girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She has such a lovely, gentle nature and we know that with time, patience and plenty of kindness, she will blossom. As she has spent more time with us, she has started to open up and show us her wonderful personality and it is so rewarding to see!

Hayley enjoys the company of other dogs and can be homed with a kind resident dog who doesn't mind sharing their space. name: Sunny
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog my size or larger to help me settle in & I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to walk on a lead and harness, but it's still very new for me.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have an undershot jaw & I have had 4 of my teeth removed during spay!

27-08-26 Sunny is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder and is trying her hardest to be brave. She was very briefly adopted, but after a few days in her new home it was clear that her and the resident dog weren't a good match and so she has returned to our care.

Sunny loves other dogs and still looks to her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she continues to grow in confidence. She will be best suited to a home where any resident dogs were her size or larger and were fairly confident and well socialised. We think she will settle quickly in the right home, and with patience and encouragement, we’re sure her lovely personality will really begin to shine.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace.She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are kind and sensible and will give her the time she needs to settle in.She will now happily approach you for a fuss and is easy to handle, which is lovely to see as she begins to settle in and discover the world around her. Sunny arrived with us very matted, but she was such a good girl during her grooming session and took everything in her stride.

Sunny has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She has started to learn all about walking on a lead and harness and though this is still new to her, she is doing well. Sunny is an amazing lady who has so much to look forward to and will make a wonderful addition to a loving and accepting home.

Sunny has arrived with an undershot jaw that does not seem to bother her, but will need to be monitored in her new home. She has had 4 teeth removed at the time of her spay.
