name: Crispin
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I could live with other dogs, or be the only dog. I don't mind. I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and love being out and about!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but returned to our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and struggled to relax in his company.

Since returning to us, Crispin has moved into foster and has settled beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be close to his people. While he can initially be worried by some men, his foster carer has found that once visitors give him some attention, he quickly relaxes and happily cuddles up with them. He does the same with female visitors. He has adult grandsons in his foster home and, after an initial bark, is very happy to settle down with them.

Crispin does get on with other dogs, but he can be quite keen to push his way in for attention and may grumble if another dog gets in the way. He is not aggressive and, having no teeth, cannot bite, but he would be best suited to either being an only dog or living with a very laid-back dog who is happy to share their space and attention. His foster carer feels he would particularly enjoy being the centre of his person's world, as he simply loves being with his human, male or female.

Crispin absolutely loves his walks and this is his favourite pastime. He gets wonderfully excited when it is time to go out and walks beautifully on both a lead and harness. He is sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places and travels well in the car. He particularly loves visiting the coffee shop and is happiest when he can be out and about with his people.

As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has settled well into a routine and sleeps soundly through the night. He has had the occasional wee indoors first thing in the morning, although this has been improving, so his adopters should continue his house training with patience and consistency.

Crispin forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite people and loves to be close by and involved in everything they are doing. He showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours, so his ideal home would be one where someone is around for most of the day and any time alone can be built up gradually.

Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing one in his left. Despite this, he gets around brilliantly and you would hardly know he has eyesight problems. He has also had all of his teeth removed and will need to remain on a soft diet for life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, which may continue to improve with gentle exercise as

Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could potentially be a little older than this.

Crispin has been given the Gift of Life by Katrina Pirner

Crispin would love a one person, male or female, calm household where he can soak up all the attention from his special human. Although he gets on with all dogs outside of the home, he prefers to be cuddled up with his human wherever it may be.. sofa, bed he s not fussed as long as he knows they are close by him.

Crispin walks perfectly on a harness and lead and is good off lead too. He will walk ahead of you but keep coming back to 'check in' with you.

Crispin continues to thrive in his foster home and is loving this home life. He loves his food, loves his walks, loves his cuddles and just loves everything to be honest.

Although Crispin lives alongside his foster sisters, I do feel he would love a home with no other dogs and just a single active  adult home, male or female, where he can have all the attention and love. Cats are fine, as he dosen't take any notice of them.

Although his initial write states that he may be older than 7 I feel he is aged about right apart from his lack of teeth as he is full of energy and  fun.

Crispin is smashing this home life. He is an absolute gentleman and will make a perfect best friend for an active person who is at home most of the time.

This week he has visited various secure fields, visited coffee shops and even popped into a pub for a cool drink while out on a street walk. He loves to be out and about with his human and then return home for snuggles on the sofa.

Although Crispin has a cataract in his right eye this does not seem to affect him at all. His luxating patellas also don't seem to bother him and his movement is 100%.

Crispin recently moved foster homes through no fault of his own. He is a gorgeous, well mannered, cuddly boy who loves his walks, his humans and his food.

He gets along with the cats and dogs in my home, though initially Crispin demanded all the attention and would push the other dogs out of the way to get his cuddles first but with careful handling this has improved over the week.

He loves to cuddle up on my bed with my own dogs and sleeps all night there. He lives for his walks and gets very excited when his lead/harness appear. He can walk on his own or with another dog for company.

He happily shares his food bowl with his foster friend Lemon Pie. Even the cats dig in with him sometimes. He is getting used to being left when I go shopping and I am extending these trips so he gets used to being without humans for a while. Crispin does bark initially when visitors come into my home but this soon subsides when he realises they will do him no harm. Keep up the good work Crispin, you've got this my boy

Crispin has been back in foster care for a week and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be loved. Sadly, he was returned because he became anxious and barked whenever the man in the household moved around.

He walks beautifully on a lead and harness, sleeps soundly through the night alongside the other foster dog, and travels well. Although he is perfectly happy living with other dogs, he could also be an only dog so he can enjoy all the cuddles and affection he deserves. He has had a few little accidents indoors first thing in the morning, but over the last few days he has settled into a much better routine.

Crispin has no teeth, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He also has a cataract in one eye and the beginnings of a cataract in the other, but you would hardly know he has any sight issues as he gets around so well.

He really is a very special little boy who simply needs a loving home where he can feel safe, secure, and cherished.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.Crispin is a dear little boy who can still be worried and unsure at times. It is clear that he had very little socialisation in the past, and although he has made lovely progress since living in a home, he still needs patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time. He can be touch-sensitive when he is feeling anxious, so gentle handling and allowing him to approach in his own time will help him continue to gain confidence.Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He would be happy to share his home with another kind and confident resident dog in his new home. However, in the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he could also be the only dog in the home.One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. Once out, he walks beautifully on a lead, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. However, he hasn't quite mastered house training yet, so his adopters will need to continue helping him learn with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. He has had dental work and unfortunately did need to have all of his teeth removed, so he will need to stay on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.Crispin is a gentle soul who has had a difficult start in life, but he has already shown that, with kindness and patience, he is capable of making wonderful progress. He is looking for a very special person who will understand his worries, celebrate his achievements, and enjoy watching him continue to blossom into the loyal and loving companion we know he can be.Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

name: Tummy
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I will need to be the only dog in the home so all of the attention is on me!

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics!

I am on a special diet for bladder stones, please read below for more information!

11-10-26 Tummy is a lovely lady who originally came to us from a breeder and was later adopted into a home. Sadly, she has returned to our care after around 5 months as she wasn't getting along with the resident dog, so she is now looking for a home where she can be the only dog and have all of her family's attention to herself. She also cannot live with cats or small furries.

Tummy is a sweet and outgoing girl with a big personality! She loves toys and having a good play, but she also enjoys a quiet fuss and relaxing alongside her people. She has lived in a home before, so she may already know some of the basics such as house training, although she may need a few gentle reminders as she settles back into home life.

Tummy would do best with a family who has experience with Dachshunds and understands their wonderful but sometimes strong personalities, although she could also live with a sensible family who are willing to learn and understand her needs. She can live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+ who are sensible and will give her the time and space she needs to settle into her new home.

Tummy has never been left home alone before and so this is something her adopters will need to build up gradually with her to ensure she doesn't develop separation anxiety.

Tummy is an amazing little lady who has already had a change of home and is now ready to find her forever family. We hope that the right home will give her the love, attention and stability she deserves.

Tummy has previously been treated for ear infections and also has some hair loss that seemed to begin to grow back when she was in her previous home. She has a history of bladder stones and is currently on a specific diet to help with this, and this will need to be continued in the home. This will need to be monitored by her new vets and her adopters will need to be aware that should she require any treatment or potential surgery in the future it would not be covered by insurance.

Hungry has been given the Gift of Life by Jacqueline Wanstall

name: Faith
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a large, extra-secure garden to keep me safe as I learn about the home.

I’m new to walking on a harness and doing well!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

Faith is a beautiful girl who came to us from a breeder and was initially incredibly shut down and terrified of people. She would run away from any human interaction and wouldn't even eat when people were around. However, over the last two months, Faith has made some wonderful progress and is slowly learning that people can be kind. She now walks on a harness, although she can still be easily spooked, and is happiest walking with people she knows and trusts. She will now take treats from us in her kennel, and sometimes on walks when things are quiet, with hot dogs being a particular favourite! Recently, she even allowed a little gentle fuss in the big play yard, choosing to stay for affection rather than run away. This may seem like a small step, but for Faith, it is a huge achievement.

Faith absolutely adores other dogs and truly comes alive when joining her friends for playtime in our big yard. She approaches them with a full-body wiggle and has even discovered how much fun toys can be, although she cannot be left unsupervised with soft toys! She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her continue building her confidence and show her the ropes of home life. As a Collie, she will also need plenty of enrichment and exercise to keep her busy once she has settled in.

Faith is still a very nervous girl who will need an adult-only home with Collie experience, where her progress will be celebrated and she can continue learning at her own pace. She has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient adopters who can help her with house training, lead walking and all the other new experiences that come with family life. She will also need an extra-secure garden of at least 6ft to keep her safe as she settles in.

Faith really is such a sweet girl who tries her very hardest to be brave. Although she is making lovely progress with us, kennels is no place for a puppy to spend these important months of her life. Her three Collie friends who arrived with her have all found their forever homes, and now it is Faith's turn to find someone who can see just how far she has come and how much potential she has. With time, patience and lots of love, we know this special girl has so much more to discover, and we desperately hope her forever family won't keep her waiting much longer.

Faith has been given the Gift of Life by Raychel Mount

name: Lucy
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Lucy is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder and is still learning that people can be kind and caring. She desperately wants to be brave but finds the world a very scary place, and can be vocal when people she doesn't know approach her. Once she gets to know you and feels comfortable with you being around, she does settle and can be calm and quiet in your presence. Lucy is such a precious girl who just needs time, patience and understanding to help her find her confidence.

Lucy is very active and playful with her kennel friends, and although she doesn't yet ask for a fuss, she will come over for a little sniff when her friends approach you. She is a girl who will need to take things at her own pace, and she has started harness training but is still learning what is expected of her. Lucy would love a home that can offer her an active lifestyle once she has had time to settle, along with at least one kind and confident resident dog who she can look to for reassurance as she learns about home life.

Lucy has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. She enjoys her food and is fed separately here, although she is happy to take treats alongside other dogs. Lucy will need an adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where her needs will be understood and she can be given the time, space and security she needs to blossom. With patience, kindness and the support of a confident canine friend, we hope Lucy will slowly learn to trust and become the most wonderful companion.

Lucy has been given the gift of life by Linda Towers

This absolutely stunning girl is Lucy and she is one girl who is absolutely breaking my heart. She desperately wants to be brave but doesn't understand that humans are actually kind and caring.

She's very unsure about people being around her that she doesn't know and can be vocal because of this, when she knows you and is happy with you existing around her then she does settle and will be calm and quiet in your presence.She needs to learn everything, she's started harness training but doesn't understand it yet and although she doesn't ask for a fuss, she will come over when her kennel friends do and have a bit of a sniff of you. She does like food and is fed separately here, but she's fine having treats with other dogs. She is honestly so precious and in the right home I can see her being the most wonderful companion, she just needs time and patience and to be kept safe in the process of gaining her confidence in this big scary world.

Lucy is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder and is understandably nervous around people. She can be quite vocal when approached and doesn’t yet enjoy being handled, she prefers to keep her distance while she works out that people can be trusted. Lucy is a sweet girl underneath her worries and will need plenty of TLC, patience and understanding from her new family as she begins to build her confidence.

Lucy is very active and playful with her kennel friends, and this is where we get to see a little more of her personality. She would love a home that can offer her an active lifestyle once she has had time to settle and feel comfortable. She will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog who she can look to and lean on for reassurance as she learns about home life and gains confidence.

Lucy has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. These things may take some time, and she will need a family who is willing to go at her pace without putting pressure on her. Lucy will need an adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where her needs will be understood and she can have the time and space she needs to blossom. With patience, love and the support of a confident canine friend, we hope Lucy will slowly learn to trust and show us the wonderful girl hiding underneath her worries.

name: Apple
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a cherry eye in my right eye and I will be spayed before adoption!

22-10-26 Apple is a shy little girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She was initially worried about being picked up, but soon found the courage to run and jump into the arms of her kennel mum. This was lovely to see and shows that, with a little reassurance, Apple can find comfort in the people she trusts. We don't think it will take her too long to settle into a loving family home, where she can begin to build her confidence and discover how wonderful life can be.

Apple gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and allow her time to settle in. Her adopters will need to have experience with ex-breeders to better understand er needs.

As Apple has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to her new surroundings.

Apple has arrived with a cherry eye, which our vets will assess and treat to ensure she is comfortable.

With a loving home, a friendly canine companion and time to settle at her own pace, we hope Apple will soon feel safe enough to let her sweet personality shine.

Apple has been given the Gift of Life by Claire Louise Oakes

name: Fanta
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand I need space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

22-10-26 Fanta is quite a scared girly who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is in need of lots of TLC and the reassurance of a confident resident dog to help her feel safe. Fanta can be a little panicky and flighty, so she will need a very secure garden with high fencing to keep her safe while she settles into her new surroundings.

Although Fanta was shaking, she allowed us to pick her up and give her a gentle fuss to reassure her that we are here to help. She is still very unsure at the moment, so her new family will need to be patient and allow her the time she needs to learn to trust.

Fanta will need another kind and confident dog in her new home, as this will be a much-needed support system for her. A reassuring canine companion can help guide her and give her the confidence she needs as she settles in and begins to find her paws.

As Fanta has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to understand that this may take time and be prepared to let her progress at her own pace. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand she needs time to settle in. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience to better understand her needs.

Fanta is a very worried little girl, but she has already shown us that she can accept gentle affection even when she is feeling frightened. We hope that with a confident canine companion, a calm environment and lots of patience, she will gradually begin to feel safe and discover the happy new life she deserves.

Fanta has been given the Gift of Life by Aimee Helme

name: Rizzle
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Rizzle is a quiet and timid girl who has come to us from a breeder. When she arrived she was quite overwhelmed and in need of plenty of TLC, but she has since started to come out of her shell.

Rizzle has recently moved to a wonderful foster home where she is settling in and starting to learn about home life for the first time ever. She is making gentle progress and is even starting to wag her tail when her fosterer speaks to her and has ventured onto the sofa twice so far, although she is understandably still quite nervous and isn't yet feeling brave enough to approach but is trying her hardest to be brave.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she begins to gain confidence and learns that the world isn’t such a scary place.

She has never lived in a home before moving to foster, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life, including house training, though she is starting to get to grips with this already. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness as she is quite worried about being handled, but hopefully this will be introduced to her in the near future.

She is a sweet little lady with so much potential and just needs someone willing to take a chance on her. With a loving home, a confident canine companion and plenty of patience, we’re sure Rizzle will slowly find her confidence and become a wonderful companion.

Rizzle has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

Rizzle is a real sweetheart, but still very nervous, moving away from me most of the time. She has just started to wag her tail when I talk to her and has twice shared the sofa, but at a distance. If she moves into a corner, I can give her a brief stroke, otherwise she will only come for a quick sniff of my hand. She is not yet confident enough to take a treat from me. She eats well, preferring to eat alone, but not because of any guarding issues.

Rizzle has chewed toys and played with Petal, my other foster dog, but this is not a regular occurrence. She spends a lot of time alongside Petal. She is getting used to household sounds, dislikes the vacuum cleaner and goes in the garden but is OK with the washing machine, and tolerates the ironing board.

Rizzle will briefly bark if she hears a sound in the garden, eg another dog or voices. At night or if I go out, she sleeps quietly in the lounge with the other dogs. She doesn't enjoy handling at the moment, so I have not made any attempt to put a harness on her. Her toilet training is a work in progress, being clean when the back door is open.

Rizzle is a quiet and timid girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is beginning to show us just how inquisitive she can be and is trying her hardest to be brave. Rizzle isn’t quite ready to approach us just yet, but she does follow the lead of her doggy friends and takes lots of comfort from having them around. With plenty of TLC, patience and reassurance, we’re sure it shouldn’t take her too long to come around and start showing her lovely personality.

Rizzle will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she begins to gain confidence and learns that the world isn’t such a scary place. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life, including house training. She will need time to take everything at her own pace and shouldn’t be rushed before she is ready.

Rizzle can live with older, dog-savvy children who are sensible and will understand that she needs time and space to settle in. She is a sweet little lady with so much potential and just needs someone willing to take a chance on her. With a loving home, a confident canine companion and plenty of patience, we’re sure Rizzle will slowly find her confidence and become a wonderful companion.

name: Twig
description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning about wearing a lead and harness.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Twig has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. When she first arrived, Twig was a very worried and flighty girl who found new people quite overwhelming and would often bark and keep her distance. However, after spending some time getting to know her, we have seen a lovely side to Twig that we knew was hiding underneath all those nerves.

Twig has now moved into a wonderful foster home where she is getting to experience home life for the very first time. She was very overwhelmed when she first moved into foster and would initially hide in the garden, but since then she has started to come out of her shell and is settling into home life and has started to unwind. She has started to bond with her fosterer and will now sit next to her on the sofa for snuggles but is still quite wary of her fosterers husband.

Twig relies heavily on the other dogs in her foster home for comfort and support and will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where there was another kind and confident resident dog to be her friend. She will need adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will help her settle in at her own pace.

Twig has recently started her harness training, although she is still very much at the beginning of this journey. She will need her adopters to take things slowly and give her plenty of time to build her confidence before expecting her to venture out into the big wide world. Lots of gentle practice in the garden will be a good place to start, and her adopters should be prepared to take things at her pace rather than rushing her. She is starting to learn all about toilet training and is doing well.

Twig is a sensitive girl who may take some time to fully trust her new family, but the progress she has already made shows us just how much potential she has. Once she knows you, she is such a sweet, gentle little lady who simply wants to be close to her person. She just needs someone willing to give her the time, patience and chance she deserves.

Twig has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

Twig or 'Twiglet' as we sometimes call her came into foster with us 2 weeks ago and it's been quite an overwhelming experience for her. She started out wanting to hide in the garden and avoiding all contact with humans. It was clear she has never had any kindness prior to coming to Many Tears and learning to live in a home environment was going to be a big challenge for her.

Despite this, she has started to unwind and is heavily relying on her other dog friends for cues and support. She has slowly formed a bit of a bond with me and we've had some really lovely snuggles on the sofa but she is still wary of my husband despite him tossing occasional snacks to her from a distance. It is clear that she is just a really scared baby that desperately wants to trust people but will be a big work in progress.

We have been able to gently get a harness on her and take her to a secure field which she enjoyed but we are still working on her lead skills without her panicking.

Twig likes having dog friends to sit with on the sofa and gets on with everyone. Her toilet training is coming along and if I go for a walk in the garden she will come too and do a wee. We are still getting a few accidents overnight though which need some patience.

Twig is not going to be a ready-to-go dog and just needs someone with the patience and time to bring her out of her shell and show her the world in small stages. Once she trusts you she really is a snuggle bug!

Twig has been with me on my section for around a month now and our bond is getting stronger and stronger by the day. When she first arrived, she was quite flighty and I could tell she was very overwhelmed, and I did think she was going to be quite a difficult one to crack to begin with. Buuuuut, thankfully I was wrong!! It did take about a week or so, but one day out of nowhere she came and sat by me .. not doing anything or making any sort of gesture .. she just sat and looked at me. I very gently started stroking her under her ear and chin, expecting her to move away, but she didn’t!!! Instead, she actually came closer to me when I stopped, as if to ask for more. From then on she’s been the same with me every day. If I’m sat down in the yard or the kennel, she’s always right next to me patiently waiting for a little fuss. She never makes any noise or fuss about it, she doesn’t barge the other dogs out of the way or get jealous, she just sits there, waiting for her turn. So sweet!!!It is a bit of a different story with strangers, however. She does still bark at them and presents as a fearful and reactive dog, but as soon as she gets to know you, that all goes away. When it’s just me and her with no other people around, she’s as quiet as a mouse. So if anyone is reading this that has seen her / or maybe will see her at the rescue, please don’t take her reaction in the kennel as face value. I promise she’s a sweet angel really!This week we have started on her harness training journey. It’s still very early days yet, but it’s a marathon and not a sprint! She hasn’t taken any steps as of yet, but I’m hoping she will after a few attempts. I would definitely recommend her future adopters do lots of practice in the garden with her before venturing out into the big wide world! Slow and steady wins the race after all.Twig would really love a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with ex breeders and will be understanding and patient with her. It may take her a little while to learn to trust fully, but I do think she will get there. She just needs someone to give her a chance.

Twig has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She can be quite vocal when first meeting new people and prefers to keep her distance, often choosing to hide away until she feels more comfortable. However, beneath her worried exterior is a lovely little lady with a very sweet nature hiding.

Twig would love a calm and understanding home where she can settle at her own pace and begin to build her confidence. She takes great comfort from her kennel friends and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can look to for reassurance as she adjusts to family life.

Twig could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that she needs a quiet environment and plenty of patience. As she has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be understanding as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. Some gentle garden sniffs may be a good place to start while she gains confidence.

Twig is a sensitive girl who is looking for a home that can offer her plenty of love, TLC, and reassurance as she discovers that the world isn't such a scary place after all.

name: Tilly
description:
I can live with older dog-savvy children who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

22-10-26 Tilly is a very sweet but extremely nervous girly who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start.

Tilly will need plenty of time to settle into her new home, as she is not comfortable being handled at the moment. name: Gail
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like a home with one kind resident dog. I cannot live with cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can walk well on a lead and harness, and am doing well with those I trust.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Gail has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived with us she was a very scared girl who found human interaction extremely overwhelming and would often hide away at the back of her kennel. It was clear that she hadn't had much socialisation before and was in desperate need of love and TLC. Since then Gail has started to come out of her shell and has made really encouraging progress. Although she is still a very nervous girl, once she gets to know you she does start to come out of her shell and will approach you for a gentle sniff and will allow you to gently stroke her, although still finds this very worrying.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to come out of her shell and settle in at her own pace. Gail is a sensitive little girl and does really struggle with change, so she is likely to go backwards in her new home at first and will need time to adjust to her new surroundings.

Gail does rely on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will be looking for a home where there is just one other kind, confident resident dog to be her friend. Gail doesn't really enjoy sharing her space with more than one dog and can be a little sassy and has shown that she much prefers just having one other dog to make her best friend. She does take a little while to warm up to other dogs, but once she bonds with them she absolutely adores them and finds confidence from them.

Gail has learned all about walking on a lead and harness since arriving with us and as long as she has a doggy friend by her side, now even goes for walks with some of our volunteers, which is very brave of her! She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her and her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles in and learns all about home life and new skills like house training.

Shortly after Gail's arrival to us, she started showing signs of back pain as well as some weakness and unsteadiness. As she's a dachshund and they can be quite prone to spinal issues, she went for x-rays to be on the safe side. The x-rays showed several mineralised discs in her spine, but did not show any obvious spinal cord compression. She was given pain relief and was put on crate rest, and initially returned to activity with the help of a supportive back brace. Gail has made a good recovery and is currently doing very well.

Gail's adopters will need to be aware that should she have any further issues in the future related to this, it would be classed as a pre-existing condition and would not be covered by insurance.

Gail is a truly special little girl who has come such a long way since arriving with us. She is still a very scared girl, and although her journey may not be a quick one, with lots of love, patience and TLC, we know it will be incredibly rewarding to watch her grow in confidence and discover just how wonderful life can be.

Gail has been given the Gift of Life by Candice Sullivan

What incredible progress this girl is making! I'm constantly impressed and surprised by her.I only work with Gail 1-2 times a month, and I'm always blown away by how far she's come when I see her again. Some things that may not seem like much can be huge milestones for our ex-breeding dogs - three months ago, Gail could only be touched by a few members of staff and was very anxious in human presence; six weeks ago, she would only tolerate having her harness put on and being walked by the two people she knew best; two weeks ago, she was walking with a few people but still spending most of her time in the back of her kennel hiding, and would try to hide in corners if she saw anyone unfamiliar; and today, she went on a 20 minute walk with me, then cuddled in my lap afterwards! She even goes for walks with volunteers she's never met before and is incredibly brave meeting new people. When visitors walk past, Gail runs to the front of her kennel with her tail wagging.Gail is a lovely little dog with so much personality. She's going to be the queen of wherever she ends up, and she deserves to be spoiled rotten! Hopefully, Gail's perfect home is right around the corner. Until then, we'll keep on showing her all the love and kindness we can.

We're super pleased with Gail's progress over the last few weeks.

Initially, we started yarding her with other dogs. She coped really well but would tell them off if they were too lively and in her face. We then started kenneling her with a female Cavalier, and she coped very well and seemed happier in herself. We then added a lively Poodle, but Gail told her off, so now she's just with the Cavalier. So, we've learnt that Gail can cope day and night with a calm dog, and on night duty, I saw them snuggled up in the same bed.Gail's walking is much better, but only with the staff who know her well. She follows her nose on a walk and likes walking in longer grass. Gail will roll over for a tummy rub but is still a little unsure about too much fuss.Gail is a happy little girl, full of character, who loves to carry her favourite toys around, and she's not possessive of them.

Gail has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a very scared little girl who found herself extremely overwhelmed when she first arrived, and it was clear she was not used to much handling or human interaction. At the beginning, Gail was very wary of people and would do her best to avoid being handled, often using warning signals to ask for space. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could panic and make poor decisions through fear. With time, patience and consistency from the staff she knows and trusts, Gail is making lovely progress and is beginning to show her softer side.

Although still a nervous girl, Gail is progressing well with the staff she has built relationships with and now enjoys attention from the people she knows well. She absolutely loves a tummy rub and has started to seek out familiar staff members for reassurance, showing that, given time, she is capable of forming strong bonds with the people she trusts.

Gail spent some time recovering from a back injury, but she is now showing no signs of pain and is back to her normal self. She happily trots around as though nothing was ever wrong and has recovered brilliantly. During her recovery she spent time on her own and, although she was later reintroduced to a previous canine friend, it became clear that Gail no longer enjoys the company of other dogs and does not like for them to invade her space. For this reason, she will need to be the only dog in her forever home.

Gail will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the importance of patience, time and reading her body language. She will need kind, understanding adopters who will allow her to take everything at a pace she feels comfortable with and continue building her confidence without putting her under pressure.

She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. She will need to learn all about home life, including house training and settling into a daily routine. Gail has also recently started her lead training and has surprised everyone with how quickly she has progressed. After taking just a few tentative steps on her first outing, she was happily trotting around, sniffing her surroundings and even confidently walking over to one of her favourite people the very next day. She is proving that, with gentle encouragement, she is capable of making wonderful progress.

As Gail has had previous back issues, we have used a supportive back brace harness to help protect her while she builds her confidence on walks. This is something her adopters may wish to continue using in the future for extra support.

Gail is a very special little girl who still has plenty to learn, but she has already shown just how far she can come with the right people by her side. She is looking for experienced adopters who are willing to invest the time and patience she needs, and in return they will gain a wonderfully rewarding companion as they watch her confidence continue to grow.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Royal
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to live with a female dog. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, and am doing so good!

Royal is a very special Chow Chow who has come to us from a breeder in search of his forever home. When he first arrived, he was extremely frightened of the world around him and was very wary of being touched or handled. Thanks to gentle care and patience, Royal has made incredible progress and is continuing to blossom in foster, where he is experiencing home life for the very first time.

Royal has exceeded all expectations with how well he has settled into foster. He has been an absolute superstar, sleeping soundly through the night, travelling well in the car, walking beautifully on lead and has even been completely clean in the house. Every day brings a new milestone, and it has been a joy to watch his confidence grow as he discovers all the comforts and pleasures of family life.

Although Royal is still nervous of people initially, he so desperately wants to trust and tries his hardest to be brave. He has begun asking his foster carers for gentle neck and bum scratches, happily takes treats from their hands, enjoys rummaging through the toy box, has found his little voice and now greets them with his wonderful wagging tail. He is such a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs time to work things out at his own pace.

Royal absolutely relies on the resident female dogs in foster for confidence and reassurance. He watches their every move, learning how to be part of a family, and loves playing alongside them. He will need to share his forever home with at least one kind, confident female dog who enjoys a good play and can continue to show him the way. He cannot live with cats.

As this is Royal's first experience of living in a home, he thrives on routine and will need patient, understanding adopters who will allow him to settle without pressure. He has made remarkable progress already, but he is still very nervous of the unknown and benefits from people who understand that he needs time to process new experiences. A calm, rural or quiet home would suit him best, as he is currently worried by traffic. He is looking for an adult-only home with breed experience and experience with very nervous rescue dogs would be highly beneficial.

Royal has recently had a bath and full groom at the rescue and was an absolute gentleman throughout. As a Chow Chow, his beautiful coat will require regular daily grooming. He is very tolerant of being brushed when it is introduced slowly, little and often, and this has become an important part of his routine.

Royal is an incredibly special boy who has embraced this new chapter in his life with quiet bravery. With patience, kindness and the continued support of confident canine companions, he will become a wonderfully loyal and loving companion. Watching him continue to discover the world and grow in confidence will be an incredibly rewarding journey, and he is sure to make his forever family smile every single day.

Royal is currently being treated for an ear infection.

Wow! This darling boy has just exceeded all expectations with how well he’s settled into his very first home, in his first week. Not a single accident (unheard of for a boy), sleeps soundly over night out of a crate, happy to be left alone with the company of the resident dogs, walks well on a lead, travels well. A literal angel boy.

Royal is the sweetest soul, he doesn’t trust humans easily but he really wants to and tries so hard to be brave.

He relies heavily on our resident girl gang for confidence & reassurance, watching & copying them intently to learn what being a member of a family is all about.

After an initial overwhelming few days for him, every day now brings a new ‘first’ & burst of joy on our part! Asking for a neck / bum scratch, taking a treat from our hand, rummaging in the toy box, playing with the girls, finding his little voice & wagging his amazing tail when we talk to him. He is just loving this next step in life and is so ready to be someone’s special boy.

Royal currently needs an adult only home as has not yet been tested with children. He needs confident kind resident female dogs who like a good play. A rural / quiet location would be preferable as he’s currently quite scared of traffic.

He is still very nervous of the unknown, thrives on routine and needs to be guided and given time to work things out without any pressure so experience with very scared dogs would be helpful.

As a Chow, his beautiful coat will need grooming daily. He is very tolerant of this if done slowly, little & often.

Please get in touch if you feel you might be the right match for this special big guy, he will make you smile every day.

Royal is not a dog I’ve had the chance to work with until recently. I’ve heard a lot about him, as he’s one of our longer stayers. I had heard many great things from other members of staff, including the incredible progress he’s made since joining us!When I did get the chance to work with him, my first impression was “oh my days, you are beautiful!” On first sight, he is one of the most beautiful dogs I’ve ever seen and certainly the most stunning chow I’ve ever seen! How can you look at this handsome boy and not fall in love?!When I actually began working with him, I realised how shy and timid he actually was. Initially, he wouldn’t come to the front of the kennel to see me, he’d hide away in the back. It was evident to me that this boy did not trust me. As I continued to work with him, I was very aware of my actions, to ensure I wasn’t causing any anxiety. I began with treats (who doesn’t love a cheeky bribe?). It slowly worked. Initially, he wanted nothing to do with me. I didn’t want to invade his safe spaces (safe spaces are so important for a more scared or anxious dog. Could you imagine a big scary stranger coming into your home and not leaving? I wouldn’t feel too easy if that occurred to me). So, I’d place the treat and leave the kennel. He’d come out, have a little nosey and take the treat. With time, he began slowly coming out of the back as I entered his kennel. He then began taking treats from my hands and now, whenever I walk onto the section, he comes straight to the gate and waits for me. Honestly, such an incredible feeling making a bond like this with such an incredible boy! There is honestly no feeling like it. They say a dog is a humans best friend but, what no one tells you it works both ways. To build that bond, teach him that I’m not scary, I’m here to help him feel safe, comfortable, happy and to get such a response… it’s honestly the best feeling in the world. Royal needs a home, he needs people to show him this on a day to day basis. We do what we can but, we can’t teach him the safety and comfort of a home, of a family that’s there for him 24/7.Once I got to know this guy a little more, I was taken away. We go out on walks. I feel like this was another bonding experience for us. He loves a walk but, loud noises and interactions with loud people/dogs do freak him out, thus we try to go for quieter walks. He also loves frolicking in the yard. From my experience, he seems to just love being outside!When I worked with him, he didn’t have a friend in his kennel, however, since working with him I have seen him enjoying in the yard with other dogs and is now kennelled with a boxer. He seems very happy. As previously mentioned on his profile, he is to be homed with females around his size or alone. I have not worked with him enough to comment further on his compatibility and amiability with other dogs so, please read the rest of his profile and updates to get a fuller understanding of this incredible boy!At this point, I’ve worked with him enough for him to trust me. He’s happy to see me, he’s fine for me to touch him and fuss him. The Royal I see is a happy dude. He is a scared dog, I’m very aware of that but, the Royal I know now is far different to the Royal I first met. You just have to gain his trust and he’ll let you see him. When you first meet him, he will be shy. He’ll hide and he will not trust you. DO NOT let this deter you. He is one of the sweetest dogs I’ve ever met. From when I first met him to now, I feel like he’s a completely different dog. I was respectful of his boundaries, slow and calm, I did what I could to make him feel comfortable and safe, he then began to trust me and show me his true self (he hides it beneath all that fur). Honestly, I love him. I will take time out of my day to go see him, give him a little treat and some love, just because he is honestly that special. I cannot believe he’s been here over a year. He is one of our most special dogs. I don’t see how anyone can get to know this dog and not love him.Don’t overlook this fluffy dude. Yes, he’s shy and nervous but, the longer you spend with him, care for him and gain his trust, the more you’ll fall in love with him. I can say with confidence; if you put the effort in with Royal, you will fall in love with him.

I absolutely love this boy with my whole heart.

I've been working hard on helping him get used to being brushed because, as a Chow, it's something his future adopters will need to keep up with regularly to keep his coat healthy and prevent mats from developing, especially behind his ears.

Royal is now an absolute angel when it comes to grooming. I brush him every day, and with it being shedding season, no matter how long I brush for, there always seems to be more fur coming out! These days, he simply finds a comfy spot, settles down, and lets me get on with it. If he's had enough, or if I come across a mat that's uncomfortable for him, he communicates so well to let me know he's done for the day.

I also recently decided it was time to give him a bath. I wasn't sure how he'd cope, as it involved picking him up and putting him in the bath, but he was an absolute angel from start to finish. He allowed me to pick him up without any fuss and stood beautifully while I bathed and shampooed him.

I'm so incredibly proud of him. Afterwards, I introduced him to the grooming blower to help remove some of his loose coat. He wasn't a huge fan of it, but he tolerated it for a short while, and I'll continue using it regularly so he can build his confidence with it.

I honestly think all this grooming time has strengthened our bond even more, because lately he seems to be seeking out so much more affection and attention from me. He's such a special boy, and it has been wonderful watching his confidence grow.

Royal has now been with us for over a year, and we’re still waiting for the right person to see just how special he is. He’s had two meet and greets during this time, but sadly neither worked out as he was too nervous meeting new families.

Royal is a sensitive boy who simply needs time, patience, and understanding. He can be unsure at first, but once he begins to trust you, his cheeky, affectionate personality really shines through and it’s such a joy to see.

With a consistent routine, Royal truly thrives. He now enjoys running freely around our large yard without a harness or lead, and when it’s time to go back, he comes straight over. He’s also been out on two longer walks away from the rescue with one of our regular volunteers and has done amazingly well.

All Royal is looking for is someone willing to give him the time and patience he deserves. In return, he’ll become a loyal and loving companion.

I’ve come on leaps and bounds over the past month. I’m still a little shy and can get nervous when I meet new people, but I’m working on it!

I feel most comfortable when I spend quality time with people. It doesn’t take long for me to start feeling at ease (though I still sometimes like my own space). The more time you spend with me, the more comfortable I become—and treats help too! I’ll return your love in equal measure, as long as I’m given the right time, support, and respect.

I love going out for walks, though I can get nervous around loud noises or sudden movements. They might make me jump or feel uneasy, but a bit of love and reassurance always helps!

I feel more comfortable every day. I benefit not only from interaction with my humans, but also from the company of my kennel friends that I live with.

Another month has gone by, and my cheeky boy Royal is still waiting in kennels. I honestly don’t know why this handsome lad isn’t getting much interest. Not only is he completely unique-looking, but he also has the funniest, quirkiest personality. If you want a dog who’ll make you laugh every single day here he is!

Royal is 99% kennel clean and always keeps his bedding tidy… well, until I make his bed perfectly for him. Then he likes to “show me how it’s supposed to be done” by pulling it all across the floor. He walks beautifully on the lead now; he can still get a little spooked from time to time, but he’s made massive progress since the day he arrived.

He loves his toys he just doesn’t love sharing them! He’s also a bit selective with kennel mates, so his ideal home would include a calm, placid large female dog who won’t make too much fuss over him.

Royal truly is an amazing boy, inside and out, and I hope he doesn’t have to wait much longer for the forever home he deserves.

Royal never fails to make us smile with his crazy, funny, and quirky personality. He’s got such a cheeky side to him just waiting for the right people to help it shine.

On the lead, Royal is already walking beautifully, though he can still get a little nervous at times. His new family will need to be patient and willing to help him build confidence. Loud noises or sudden movements can overwhelm him, so he’ll do best with calm, quiet walks to start.

This week Royal had his very first trip down to the big yard! He loved it, though he found his confidence by sticking close to his doggy friend. With more practice, we’re sure he’ll begin to explore on his own.

Royal absolutely adores other dogs. Once he’s settled in, he loves to play, so he’ll need a kind and confident resident dog to show him the ropes, give him reassurance, and of course, enjoy plenty of playtime together.

He’s such a handsome boy with so much love to give we can’t believe he hasn’t found his forever home yet!

This past month has been a huge step forward for our boy Royal! Once a little unsure of the world, Royal is now walking beautifully on lead, it’s such a massive step for him considering how nervous he once was!

Royal currently shares his kennel with both a male and a female dog and he’s proving to be a respectful and easy companion. He enjoys their company, often watching what they do and following their lead. Royal will definitely need another resident dog around his size in his home, so he can continue to have the doggy companionship to help him continue to grow in confidence.

Despite his progress, Royal is still a sensitive soul, and it takes a little time for him to warm up to you. Royals forever family will need to give him time and patience to come out of his shell, so for this reason I believe Royal would be best suited to a home with no children.

Please don’t leave Royal waiting much longer for his forever home, he really deserves a cosy sofa to curl up on!

I’m so proud of Royal, this boy has come on tremendously since arriving at Many Tears. From arriving a terrified dog and very unsure of us humans, he has now slowly but surely begun to trust us and realise we are not so bad, especially when we arrive with cheesy treats.

Royal loves food, toys and being outside in our yards. He has just began harness training, ready to begin lead walking. At the moment he is not so keen on lead walking but he has taken a few tentative steps and with the help of some squeezy cheese and possibly a confident doggie friend to follow I think it won’t be long before he can begin to enjoy exploring the world.

Royals adopters will need to understand he is still very wary and unsure of his environment and he is going to need plenty of time, love and patience to trust his humans, but in the right home and given time I think this boy is going to be a big, playful and lovable boy. Royal will need a home where there is already a resident dog.

Royal is a very scared boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is especially scared when it comes to being touched by us humans but when you get him in the back of the kennel he will allow you to gently stroke him but he is uncomfortable with this. At the moment Royal could possibly make the wrong decision if handled incorrectly but this is purely through fear and he is already starting to make improvements. He will actually get excited to see his kennel mum in the mornings and will wag his tail but he’s not sure how to interact with her yet.

Royal has never lived in a home so this is going to be completely overwhelming at first and he will definitely need at least one other dog in the home to help his confidence. This will help him with house training and lead walking but these are things that are going to take him time to learn as the garden may be as scary as the home at first.

Royal will need a very calm and quiet, adult only home and adopters who have lots of experience with scared dogs. We think he’ll come out of his shell a lot more over time but Royal needs a lot of TLC, time and patience.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Irene
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas.

21-10-26 Irene is a nervous little lady who has come to us from a breeder. Although she is still unsure, she shows lovely glimpses of wanting to be confident. If you are patient with her and crouch down to her level, she'll quietly come over to give you little kisses, showing just how much love she has to give once she feels safe.

Irene will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she learns about trust and settles into home life. She has recently moved to a foster home where she is learning all about the routines of home life. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in. She will need a home that has experience with ex-breeders that can provide her with the assurance she deserves.

Irene is new to lead walking but has enjoyed plenty of walks with her foster mummy and is gaining her confidence on the lead. She will need a home without cats as she has met cats while out and about and was a little too interested in them. Irene is a truly lovely girl who just needs time, patience and plenty of TLC. With an understanding home and a canine friend by her side, we're sure she will continue to grow in confidence and become a wonderful companion.

Irene has been assessed by our vets who have noted that she has Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas. These aren't causing her any issues at the moment and may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. They will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet and her adopters should be aware that any future treatment relating to her luxating patellas will not be covered by insurance.

Irene has been given the Gift of Life by Trudie Williams

name: Cooper
description:
I would like a calm and quiet, adult only home in a semi-rural area.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I don't mind cats!

I would love a good sized garden to explore and will need 6ft fences.

I am a beginner to walking on a lead, but would like an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home! Read below for more!

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who was extremely overwhelmed when he first arrived. Although he is still feeling quite overwhelmed to find himself here and can be very worried, especially in new situations, he is making good progress, especially with those people he knows. He was initially very worried when he first met new people, but his circle of friends has grown and he is making more human friends daily. With his favourite people, he is a friendly, affectionate boy.

Cooper will be looking for a home with adopters with experience of scared rescue dogs and though not essential, experience with Romanian rescue dogs would be a bonus. He would be happiest in a calm, quiet, adult only home where he can settle in at his own pace and continue building his confidence. Cooper would be best suited to a home in a rural or semi-rural location and would prefer to go for walks in quiet areas. He will need a secure garden with 6ft fences.

Cooper is especially worried when he finds himself in new or unfamiliar areas, and busy environments with lots of noise, people and hustle and bustle can feel particularly overwhelming for him. He finds visiting the front of the rescue and reception area quite daunting, where there is more activity and unfamiliar sights and sounds. However, when he is given the chance to spend time in a quieter, open yard, he is much more relaxed and happy, showing us that he does best when he has space and a calm environment around him.

Cooper absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort from having canine friends around him, so he will need another kind, confident and playful resident dog in his new home to be his companion and show him the ropes. He is also beginning to discover the joy of toys and is enjoying learning how to play, which is so sweet. He has met cats at the rescue fine, and we may consider homing him with a dog-savvy cat.

As Cooper has never lived in a home before, his adopters will need to be patient, kind and understanding while he settles in and learns all about home life, including new skills like house training. He is very much a beginner when it comes to walking on a lead and harness, but he is already starting to enjoy his walks and would love an active home where he can continue exploring the world at his own pace.

With patience, understanding and plenty of love, Cooper will start to discover just how wonderful his life can now be. In return, this gentle boy will reward his family with the privilege of watching him blossom into the happy and loved companion he was always meant to be. He will require multiple meet and greets with his potential adopters to give him plenty of time to get comfortable with his new family.

He is currently being monitored for left back leg lameness, and has a potential soft tissue injury. He will continue to be monitored by our vets for any further treatment he may need.

He has tested negative prior to arrival for heartworm, lyme disease, ehrlichia, anaplasma, giardia, leishmania and brucellosis.

It’s been just over a month since I last did an update on our handsome boy Cooper and since then his confidence has grown even more!

Cooper is now the centre of attention in our big play group, he will engage in play with all the dogs who attend, and even greet any new ones with very good manners! Cooper is also now making lots of human friends with numerous members of staff that he used to be scared of!!

It’s absolutely crazy to see how confident Cooper is being, compared to the day he first arrived! It just goes to show all it take is time, patience and love!

I literally love Cooper with all my heart, watching him turn into the happiest, friendliest boy makes my heart so full!

I really hope his time to be in a home comes soon, he really does have so much love to give when he knows you!

When Cooper first arrived, his world was filled with fear. He would quietly tuck himself away at the back of his kennel, very unsure of all his surroundings and who we all were. It was so heartbreaking to see how scared cooper really was.

But every day, with kindness, patience and love, Cooper has taken another tiny step forward. Those tiny steps have turned into giant leaps. Today, the Cooper who once hid away greets his kennel mum with a wagging tail every morning and spends his days happily playing or relaxing with his kennel friends. His personality is really staring to come through and he is slowly learning that the world isn't such a scary place.

When Cooper first arrived, he'd had very little experience walking on a lead. Now he is improving so much more, he even happily takes trips down to our big play yard!

Cooper still finds unfamiliar places and new people a little scary, but it doesn't take long for him to realise he's safe. Once he trusts you, you see the sweetest, gentlest soul who simply wants to love and be loved.

Cooper has done everything we've asked of him. He's been brave. He's learned to trust. He's opened his heart. Now, we're asking for someone to do the same for him.

This beautiful young boy shouldn't be growing up behind kennel doors. He should be learning about the world from the comfort of a sofa, chasing toys around a garden, falling asleep after long walks, and knowing what it feels like to be in a home.

I am so incredibly proud of the progress Cooper has made and I have no doubts in a home with all the patience and kindness he will blossom into the most amazing loving family member anyone could wish for.

name: Dora
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog who is larger than me in my new home.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I have spent some time in a home so may know the basics.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

02-10-26 Dora is a very worried little girl who originally came to us from a breeder. She spent around 10 months with us before being adopted, but sadly, after only a few months with her adopters, Dora has returned to Many Tears due to a change in their circumstances.

Dora is still finding the world a very overwhelming place and will need a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with very scared ex-breeding dogs. She will need lots of patience, understanding and gentle encouragement as she continues to learn that the world can be a safe place.

Dora relies heavily on other dogs for confidence and comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can be her friend and help show her the ropes. She would be best suited to a resident dog who is larger than her. Having already experienced living in a home, Dora has made some lovely progress, but moving to a new environment will still be a big change for her. She will need plenty of time and TLC to settle and may need some gentle reminders about her house training while she gets used to her new routine.

Dora has come a long way and will now allow you to gently stroke her, provided you take things slowly and give her the choice to approach. She is still very unsure of being handled and does not enjoy being picked up or having her harness put on or taken off, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding of this. She is very food motivated, however, and will happily come over for some tasty paste, so this could well be the way to Dora's heart!

Once she is wearing her harness, Dora can walk nicely on a lead. She will need adopters who understand that progress for a worried little dog like Dora can take time, but with kindness, patience and the reassurance of a confident canine friend, we hope she can continue to blossom.

Dora is looking for a very special home where she can be given the time, TLC and understanding she needs. She has already shown that she is capable of making progress, and we hope that with the right family by her side, she can continue to build her confidence and enjoy all the lovely things that life has to offer.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Jules
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I will need a kind resident dog in my new home. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 32 teeth removed and will need a soft food diet.

21-09-26 Jules has come to us from a breeder to start her new adventure. She is a very nervous girl who is feeling overwhelmed by all the changes in her world. She is unsure of people and worried about being handled, so will initially run away and hide. She is a sweet girl underneath her worries, and we hope that with kindness, reassurance and time, she will slowly learn that people can be trusted.

Jules will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need to settle in completely at her own pace. We would consider a home with gentle, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who can give her the space and patience she needs.

Jules will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe as she adjusts to home life. Having a canine friend to learn from will be important for Jules as she begins to build her confidence and discover that the world isn't such a scary place.

Jules has never lived in a home before, so she will need kind and patient adopters as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She will also need to learn about walking on a lead and harness, starting with gentle practice around the garden and gradually building her confidence.

Jules is a sweet girl who has so much potential, and in the right home, we hope she will truly thrive. With patience, understanding and the support of a confident canine companion, she can begin to feel safe and discover just how wonderful life can be.

Our vets have noted that Jules has ectropion affecting her lower eyelids, which has been assessed but required no treatment. She has had 32 teeth removed at the time of her spay and will need a soft food diet moving forwards.

Jules has been given the Gift of Life by Susan Stacey

name: Kirk
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have been neutered and am ready for my forever home.

30-09-26 Kirk is a scared young lad who has come into our care from a breeder. He is not used to being handled, but he will accept us picking him up and, once he is settled in our arms, he seems to really enjoy a gentle fuss.

Kirk is currently kennelled with another male dog, but we think he would be fine to be homed with a suitable female too. We believe that Kirk will need another dog in his new home, and this canine companion will be a much-needed support system for him as he settles in and begins to find his confidence.

As Kirk has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. His new family will need to be patient and understanding while he gets used to all the new experiences that come with living in a home. He can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 13+ who are sensible.

Kirk has arrived with matted fur, so he will be having a much-needed groom to help him feel more comfortable and start to feel a little more like himself.

Kirk is a sweet young boy who is understandably unsure at the moment, but we can already see that he enjoys affection once he feels safe. We hope that with the support of a kind canine companion, a patient family and plenty of TLC, he will slowly grow in confidence and enjoy the happy new start he deserves.

Kirk has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter
