name: Hooper
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and have had an entropion repaired on my left eye.

21-09-26 Hooper is a very handsome gentleman who has come to us from a breeder. He can be a little on the nervous side, especially when meeting new people, but he is growing in confidence every day and we are beginning to see more of his lovely personality. Hooper is starting to trust the familiar faces he sees regularly, although he can still be unsure when someone new approaches him and may retreat to the back of his kennel where he feels safest.

Hooper shares his kennel wonderfully with his doggy friends and really enjoys having them around him. He will need at least one calm and confident resident dog in his new home that he can lean on and look to for reassurance as he continues to build his confidence. Having a friendly dog by his side will be a big help to Hooper as he learns that the world isn't such a scary place.

Hooper can live with older, sensible, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that he is a nervous boy and will give him the time and space he needs to settle in. He isn't walking on a lead yet, so his adopters will need to be patient as he learns this new skill. For Hooper, some quiet garden sniffs may be the perfect place to start while he gets used to his new surroundings before gradually building up to adventures further afield.

Hooper has never lived in a home before, so there will be lots for him to learn. His adopters will need to be kind and patient as he learns about house training and all the new sights, sounds, routines and experiences that come with home life. He will need someone who understands that his progress may take time and who will allow him to move at his own pace without putting pressure on him.

Hooper will need adopters with previous ex-breeding experience who understand the patience and understanding these dogs can require. He isn't going to be the sort of dog who walks straight into a new home and feels completely at ease, but we know that with the right person, he has the potential to make some amazing progress.

Hooper really needs someone to take a chance on him and show him just how wonderful life can be. He is a gentle boy who is slowly learning to trust, and we hope that the right family will see the lovely dog underneath his nerves and give him the time, patience and love he deserves.

He has had an entropion repaired on his left eye.

Hooper has been given the Gift of Life by Jackie Coleman

name: Pop
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy kids aged 13+ who love cuddles, and are active!

I will need to be the only pet in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I would like a secure garden where I can have plenty of play time!

I am very active and will need a home that will take me on plenty of adventures!

I may have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics.

I have been spayed and am ready to find my forever home!

Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to “Pop”, so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise and mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is a quick learner who has mastered “sit” and is currently learning “touch”. She picks things up quickly, which is helping with her ongoing muzzle training.

Pop walks beautifully on her harness and would happily walk for miles, so she will need an active home that enjoys getting out and about and helping her learn new things. She is doing well with her training and is now walking alongside calm dogs, which is lovely progress. However, she is not yet comfortable wearing a muzzle for long periods, and we are continuing to build her confidence with this gradually. The aim is to help her become comfortable wearing one when needed, so she can be kept safe around other dogs in busier areas in the future. At the rescue, under supervision with her surroundings managed, she is enjoying muzzle free play time with Lassie so it is possible she will not always need a muzzle for mixing with her canine friends.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Although she is making progress with carefully managed walks alongside calm dogs, she can still become reactive when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and committed to continuing her positive, reward-based training to help her feel more comfortable around dogs when out and about.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine. She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle, ongoing training and consistency she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

Pop has been making really good progress and has even made a friend here that she mixes with unmuzzled, she seems to enjoy a little bit of a play but then needs to have a little pause during some play dates when her friend gets a little bit too playful and overwhelms her. After a couple of minute of calm she will happily play again but it's important that her new people don't rush her with her socialisation, and instead, just take it at a pace that Pop is happy and comfortable with. She is very good at communicating when she's feeling a bit overwhelmed so you just have to listen to her and take her out of the stressful situation.

We are still muzzle training her to help her with her doggy social skills, this is very much a work-in-progress as we want her to be 100% happy with one step before moving on to the next, but I am very proud of her for reaching the stage of putting her nose in on queue and holding it there for a few seconds before getting more tasty paste.

In general she is such a happy ball of energy who just wants someone who will take her on adventures and truly be her best friend.

Pop can be homed with dog-savvy teens but they must be understanding of her getting a little mouthy when over-excited and although this is something that she is improving on, we don't want her new adopters to be worried by this behaviour if it were to happen in the home. We ignore it and reward her for being calm, which is all it usually takes for her to stop and then we continue with something fun, she also will usually grab a toy when excited in her kennel, so we are in the process of teaching her to do this on command to help her know where to place all that excited energy safely.

I can see her making a family incredibly happy, she really does have so much to offer the right home.

Pops is such a beautiful, smart girl who is super friendly with people. She has just mastered "sit" and is currently learning "touch". She picks things up pretty quickly, which is also helping her with her muzzle training.

Pops isn't sociable with other dogs currently, but this is something we're working on by taking her on walks with calm dogs at a distance. Once she is happily muzzle trained, we will work up to safe mixes with dogs who are a good match.

She does need to be an only dog in the home, and her people will need to keep up the training we've put in place to help her feel more comfortable around other dogs when out and about in public.

She walks absolutely beautifully on her harness and would happily walk for miles and miles, so she will need an active home who enjoys helping their dog feel happier and learn new things.

Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to "Pop", so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is a wonderful little girl who is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate, sweet nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise as well as mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is doing well with her lead walking and enjoys getting out and about, but she will need owners who are committed to continuing her training and helping her build confidence.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Whilst she can walk past some dogs, she is worried by them and can become reactive on lead, making the wrong choices when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and willing to continue working on her doggy social skills using positive, reward-based training. We have already started muzzle training with Pop to help build her confidence, with the hope that, in time, she may be able to enjoy controlled walks alongside calm canine companions.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine.

She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a truly wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle and ongoing training she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

name: Koala
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and have had 4 teeth extracted,

Koala relies heavily on her kennel friends for confidence and comfort, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and help her feel more secure. Having a canine friend by her side will be very important as she begins to experience life outside of kennels.

Koala has never lived in a home before, so she will need understanding adopters who can give her the time she needs to settle in and learn about house training. Lead walking may be far too scary for her initially, so she will need a secure garden where she can safely explore, sniff and build her confidence at her own pace.

Koala can live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who are sensible and understand that she will need plenty of space and patience. Her adopters will need previous ex-breeding experience so they can better understand her needs and help her adjust to life in a home.

Koala is a very frightened girl, but underneath her worries is a little lady who deserves the chance to learn how wonderful life can be. She is looking for someone special who is willing to take a chance on her and give her the time she needs to blossom.

Koala has had 4 teeth extracted at the time of her spay.

name: Geneva
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Geneva has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home and, like many of our ex-breeding dogs, is still learning that people can be kind. She has come a long way during her time at Many Tears, although she still finds human touch worrying and is not yet comfortable with being handled. She lives in a kennel where she can move freely between her kennel and the yard without needing to be picked up, allowing her to feel safe and secure in her surroundings.

We recently tried to begin harness training with Geneva, but she wasn't quite ready as she still found being touched too frightening. However, she has now taken a lovely little step forward! With the colder weather arriving, Geneva has tolerated having a cosy sweater put on, kindly knitted and donated by one of our lovely volunteers to help keep our underweight dogs warm. Although she was still a little anxious, with encouragement from a furry friend, she allowed us to put it on. This is a huge achievement for Geneva and shows that, with time and reassurance, she is slowly beginning to learn that not all human interaction has to be scary.

Geneva will need a calm and quiet adult home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need plenty of time, patience and TLC to settle in. We would consider a home with calm and respectful teenagers aged 16+. She will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog to help show her the ropes and give her reassurance as she learns about home life.

Geneva has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient adopters who can help her learn all about house training, wearing a harness and walking on a lead at her own pace. She has so much to learn, and her progress may be slow to begin with, but she deserves the chance to discover how wonderful life can be.

Geneva is such a sweet little soul, and we hope her forever family is out there waiting for her. She has already taken some brave little steps forward, and with the right home, a confident canine friend and lots of kindness, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and feel safe enough to let her lovely personality shine.

Geneva has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

In the time Geneva has been at Many Tears, she's come a long way! Like a lot of our ex-breeders, Geneva is still shy of handling, so she lives in a kennel where she can run between her kennel and the yard without having to be picked up.A few weeks ago, we started harness training with Geneva, but unfortunately she was not ready for it as she still found human touch too frightening. However, with the drop in temperature this week, Geneva has tolerated having a sweater put on her! This sweater was knitted by a lovely volunteer and donated to the rescue, and helps keep underweight dogs like Geneva warm through autumn and winter. Although she was anxious being handled, Geneva is beginning to learn that not all humans are bad, so with encouragement from her best friend Tammy the westie, she let me put her sweater on!This is a huge step for Geneva, and fingers crossed her people can help her feel even more safe and secure.

Geneva has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a worried little girl who is feeling quite overwhelmed by all the changes in her world and is going to need lots of love, patience and TLC from her new family. Geneva isn't used to being handled and it is clear that she hasn't had much socialisation in her life so far. She finds being picked up and handled quite worrying, but once she is safely in your arms she does settle and seems to enjoy having a gentle stroke. She is a sweet girl who just needs someone to show her that people can be kind and that the world isn't such a scary place.

Geneva will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who understand that she will need to settle in at her own pace. We would consider a home with teenagers aged 16+ who are calm and respectful around dogs.

She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness, so she will need to practise wearing these around the home and garden first, gradually building her confidence before she is ready to venture further afield. Her new family will need to take things at her pace and understand that progress may be slow to begin with.

Geneva is a sweet little soul who has so much to learn, but with the right home, a kind resident dog and patient adopters, we hope she will blossom into a happy and confident little companion. She needs someone who will see the frightened girl she is today and be willing to give her the time and love she needs to discover just how wonderful life can be.

Geneva arrived with us showing signs of a urine infection and possible bladder stones. She has been treated for the urine infection and has had multiple small bladder stones removed.

name: Gigi
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I need a resident dog Cocker Spaniel size or larger to be my friend.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Gigi is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder. When she first arrived, she was terrified of people and would try to escape any area she was in if she thought someone might approach her. Thankfully, she has made lovely progress and is now much more relaxed around the carers she knows. She has settled into her routine and will even come over for little sniffs when her kennel friends approach for attention. She is also much easier to handle now and, when worried, will retreat to her safe corner rather than trying to flee.

Despite her progress, Gigi remains a flight risk and her safety must always be a priority. Her adopters will need to be very safety-conscious and have a very secure garden with fencing at least 6ft high. Moving to a new environment may cause her confidence to regress, so precautions will be essential to keep her safe. We hope to begin harness training with her, but this will need to be introduced slowly and carefully. Double-leading will be absolutely essential for a long time to come.

Gigi absolutely loves other dogs and is delighted to meet them, wanting to be friends with everyone! She will need a kind, confident resident dog who genuinely enjoys canine company and can take her under their wing, helping her feel secure and guiding her through the different aspects of home life. She will need this dog to be Cocker Spaniel sized or larger and cannot be homed with smaller dogs.

As Gigi has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who can help her learn about house training, lead walking and all the new experiences that come with being a much-loved pet. She needs an adult-only home with experience of ex-breeding dogs, where her fears are understood and she is given the time, space and reassurance she needs to settle at her own pace.

Gigi has come a long way already, and with the right home, a loving canine companion and plenty of time and patience, we believe she has the potential to continue blossoming. Her new family must be prepared to put in as much time and effort as she needs, taking everything slowly and steadily so she can learn that life can be a wonderful place to be.

Gigi has been given the Gift of Life by Rachel Morris

When Gigi was first moved in to her current section she was terrified, she would try to jump out of any area she was in if she felt a human may be getting near to her, now she has settled into the routine and knows the carers of the section well, she is far more relaxed with them, even coming up for little sniffs when her kennel friends do. She is much easier to handle now too and will freeze in her safe corner in her kennel rather than trying to flee.

Despite the progress she has made her new adopters will be very safety conscious with a very secure garden to ensure that if she were to regress when brought in to a new environment she would always still be safe. We feel that with the progress she has made we can now start to harness train her, this will be a slow process always keeping her safety at the forefront of our minds and double leading her will be absolutely essential for a long time to come.

Gigi loves other dogs, any dog she meets makes her very happy and she truly wants to be a friend to them all, so she will need a resident dog who actively loves having a companion and will really take her under their wing and help to guide her through all aspects of home life.

In the right home she will thrive but her new humans will need to be prepared to put in as much time, effort and patience as she needs and to take it slow and steady so she truly learns to see that life is actually pretty good after all.

Gigi is a very worried lady who has come to us from a breeder and is understandably very nervous and uncomfortable around people. She can be considered a flight risk as she will do her best to get away when she feels worried, so she will need very slow and gentle introductions to the world around her.

Gigi is going to need lots of TLC, patience and understanding from her new family as she learns that she is safe and begins to build her confidence. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on for reassurance as she settles in.

Gigi has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. These things may take some time, and she will need a family who is happy to let her progress at her own pace. She will need a very secure garden with fences 6ft+.

Gigi will need an adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where her needs can be understood and she can receive the patience and reassurance she deserves. With time, love and the support of a confident canine companion, we hope Gigi will slowly learn to trust and become the happy, active girl we know she can be.

name: Iggy
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas.

Iggy is a scared little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has now been with us for almost two months and, although she has made some lovely progress, she has had very little interest so far.

Iggy's biggest fear is being touched. When someone reaches for her, she can crouch down and tremble with fear, but she is slowly learning that people can be kind and that she is safe. She is beginning to show more interest in people and, by watching the other dogs around her, has started running towards her carers' hands and giving them a little boop! She has also started taking treats, which is a huge step forward for this very special girl.

Iggy takes great comfort from her kennel friends and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her build confidence, learn to trust and discover the joys of home life. She absolutely loves being out in the yard with her friends and enjoys nothing more than rolling around in the sunshine.

As Iggy has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns about house training and settles into a new routine. She is still new to lead walking and will need continued, gentle encouragement as she learns. She will need adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs who understand how frightened she can be and are prepared to give her plenty of time and patience.

Iggy can live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+ who are sensible and able to allow her to settle at her own pace.

Iggy has been assessed by our vets and has Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas. These are not causing her any issues at present and may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. They will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet, and they should be aware that any future treatment relating to her luxating patellas will not be covered by insurance.

Iggy is a wonderful girl who has already shown us that, with the right canine companion and plenty of patience, she can take those important little steps forward. We hope the right family will give her the chance to continue blossoming and discover how lovely life can be.

Iggy has been given the Gift of Life by Susan Stacey

This wonderful girl is Iggy! It’s been almost two months since she arrived, and although she is doing incredibly well, sadly she has had very little to no interest so far.

As a Frenchie / Bulldog lover myself, I took to this girl instantly, and she has now moved into my section. She has settled in so well and walks beautifully on her harness.

Iggy’s biggest fear is being touched. When someone reaches for her, she crouches down as though she wishes the ground would swallow her up, and she trembles with fear. Every day, I sit beside her in her kennel and gently stroke the side of her face, reassuring her that she doesn’t need to be afraid anymore. She is slowly learning that not everyone is there to hurt her, but I can only imagine what this poor girl may have experienced in her life.

What makes her progress even more special is seeing her learn from the other dogs around her. When they come over for fuss, Iggy has started running towards my hands and giving them a little boop! She has even started taking treats, which is a huge step for this very special girl.

Iggy absolutely loves being out in the yard with her friends. She enjoys nothing more than rolling around in the sunshine, and I could happily sit and watch her all day when she’s feeling relaxed and happy.

But as wonderful as her time here has been, I know that what Iggy truly needs now is a home of her own. A quiet, patient and understanding home where she can continue to learn that the world isn’t such a scary place, at her own pace, surrounded by people who will never give up on her.

name: Archie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 21 teeth removed.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive and patient way.

He is a cuddly and affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

As Archie has lived in a home before, he will already be familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. However, he may need a little reminding of his house training in a new environment. He walks well on a lead and enjoys his walks with volunteers.

Archie is looking for a quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of the breed and of rescue dogs. He will need people who are happy to give him the time and space he needs to settle and understand that he is safe.

Archie is doing really well since returning to us and his confidence is growing all the time. He is such a loving little dog, and in the right home, we hope he will continue to thrive and become a devoted companion.

Archie is an absolute pleasure to work with! It’s been some time now, and our bond continues to grow stronger every day.He absolutely loves smothering you with kisses and will do anything to get himself onto your lap! Archie has been kennelled with a few dogs and socialised with plenty more, but he has become particularly taken with a Cocker called Trixie. They share some similar traits, including not wanting to share their humans, although neither has displayed any jealousy towardsthe other so far. They absolutely love running laps around the yard together before heading straight into your lap for some fuss. Archie will even stand on Trixie’s back just to make sure he gets in on the action and doesn’t miss out on any attention!As mentioned, Archie is yet to display any jealous traits towards either dogs or humans, but that doesn’t mean he won’t potentially show this once settled into a home. It’s something any potential adopter should be mindful of and prepared to manage appropriately.

What I can promise, though, is that Archie will become your best friend. He has so much love to give and, once he trusts you, he will love you unconditionally.This gorgeous boy deserves someone who will give him the love, patience and understanding he needs — and in return, you’ll have a loyal companion who will want nothing more than to be by your side.

Archie is the funniest and cheekiest of little Dachshunds. Archie needs a little time to warm to you (but not all that long), and once he does, he is the most lovely of boys. I have been caring for him for a few weeks now, and I am totally smitten.

Archie walks beautifully on lead and loves nothing more than when we venture out for a stroll along the lanes around the rescue. Archie is very fond of his toys and will happily run around the yard with a ball in his mouth. He will also spend much time organising his cuddly toys, making sure they are in just the right place.

Archie has been kennelled with other small female dogs. He seems to do best with robust smaller females, as he can be a little frisky with the more timid dogs. Archie could go as an only dog in the right home, one where there are humans who will have lots of time for him.

Archie is very enthusiastic with his kisses once he knows you and will desperately clamber over you for fusses. Archie is an all-round lovely little dog, best suited to a quiet adult home where there is plenty of love, time, and patience for him to truly settle in.

Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive, patient way.

He is a cuddly, affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

Archie is a gorgeous little boy who came to us from a breeder and was understandably unsure of the world around him. It was truly heartbreaking to see how frightened he was as he would shy away from human contact and retreat when approached. Archie needs gentle handling, patience, and calm, slow movements to help him feel safe. Already, we are seeing progress. He enjoys a gentle fuss and has grown some confidence wagging his tail enthusiastically.

He gains reassurance from other dogs and will need a kind, confident resident dog in his new home to help guide him, boost his confidence, and show him that people and home life can be safe and rewarding.

Archie has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he learns the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. He could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and his own space to settle in.

Since arriving with us, Archie has undergone extensive and much-needed dental treatment and has had 21 teeth removed. He is now recovering well and feeling much more comfortable.

name: Ursula
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can now walk on a lead and harness, but need more practice.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, but will need more training.

I have a bilateral Grade 2 patella luxation.

Ursula is a sweet little lady who has come into our care from a breeder and is now enjoying life in a foster home, where she has been starting to experience home life for the first time ever. She is still slowly coming out of her shell and can easily become overwhelmed by new situations, but overall she is a very gentle girl who is making steady progress. When she does become worried, she can panic and may choose to make the wrong decision purely out of fear. On occasion, she has nipped when frightened, so she will need understanding adopters who can recognise when she is feeling overwhelmed and give her the gentle support she needs.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace.

Ursula takes comfort from having a kind and confident dog around her and will need a resident dog in her new home who can help her understand that new things are not always scary. She would benefit greatly from having a canine companion to look to for reassurance as she continues to settle and build her confidence. With the right support, we are sure Ursula will continue to become more comfortable and show her lovely personality.

Ursula had never lived in a home before moving to her wonderful foster home, but she is already doing wonderfully with her house training in her foster home. She happily sleeps through the night without any accidents and is essentially house trained, which is fantastic progress. Her adopters will still need to be patient and understanding as she continues to learn about home life and build her confidence.

She has started learning to walk on a lead and harness and though she still needs more practice to build up her confidence, she is doing well.

Ursula was underweight when she arrived but is gradually gaining weight and becoming healthier and stronger. She is a gentle little girl who needs a calm and understanding home where she can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. She may still become overwhelmed from time to time, but she is learning that she is safe and that her people will be there to reassure her.

Ursula has bilateral Grade 2 luxating patellas, but with gentle exercise this is currently not causing her any problems. Her adopters will need to be aware that this is a pre-existing condition and a disclaimer will apply, meaning it would not be covered by insurance. She also arrived with an umbilical hernia, which has since been repaired during her spay.

Ursula is a sweet and gentle little girl who has already made some lovely progress during her time in foster. She will need a family who can offer her patience, kindness and plenty of reassurance as she continues to find her confidence. With a kind resident dog by her side and a calm, loving home, we are sure Ursula will blossom into a wonderful companion.

Ursula has been given the Gift of Life by Anne Breen

Ursula has now had an amazing groom and looks like the poodle she is. So far Ursula has had no interest at all and I don’t understand why.

This baby is only 3 but has already seen things she struggles to forget. She’s only now understanding that hands can mean treats or gentle strokes and are nothing to worry about.

She’s now out walking with her doggy friends and loves all those smells. She is still nervous when someone approaches but I’m sure that will slowly pass once she realises they only want to say hello.

Ursula does easily panic and when this happens she doesn’t always make the right decision but with a calm voice and gentle hands she calms down.

She so deserves a calm and gentle household and relies on my resident dogs. So will require a friendly resident dog in her forever home.

Ursula has now been in foster for just over a fortnight and is still slowly coming out of her shell. She’s a very gentle girl but can easily get overwhelmed. When this happens she does tend to make the wrong decisions, but calms down fairly quickly.

She is gradually increasing her weight as she was underweight when she arrived.

Ursula will need a kind and gentle resident dog to help her understand new things are not always bad. Ursula happily sleeps through the night without any accidents and basically house trained. She has been diagnosed with grade 2 luxating patellas but with gentle exercise it’s not causing her any problems. She will have a disclaimer for this problem.

Ursula is a sweet little lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is confident enough to come over and greet you when you approach, but she can lose confidence when it comes to being handled and may retreat until she feels safe again. With patience and gentle reassurance, she is continuing to grow in confidence every day.Ursula could be the only dog in a home, provided her adopters have plenty of time to help build her confidence and support her as she settles into family life. She could also happily live with a kind and confident resident dog who she can look to for reassurance as she learns about home life and continues to gain confidence.Having never lived in a home before, Ursula will need patient and understanding adopters to help her with house training and lead walking and all the new experiences that come with family life.Ursula is a gentle, affectionate little lady who simply needs a family willing to give her the time she deserves. With kindness, patience, and understanding, she is sure to blossom into a wonderful companion.Ursula has arrived with a bilateral Grade 2 patella luxation that may improve with gentle exercise but will need to be monitored in the home. Her adopters will need to be aware of this as it may not be covered by insurance. She has also arrived with an umbilical hernia that has been repaired during her spay.

name: Pushkin
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on harness but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home. Read below for more information!

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She can be nervous when meeting new people and situations, but her confidence has grown so much during her time with us. She simply needs a little time to warm up and figure people out, and once she feels comfortable her wonderful personality starts to shine through.

Pushkin is a truly lovely girl with a fun, quirky nature and a very affectionate side. She has become a firm favourite with the staff who know her, and once she trusts you she is incredibly rewarding to spend time with. She loves being around people she knows and has a gentle, sweet temperament that is impossible not to fall in love with.

Pushkin takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help guide her through life. She gets along beautifully with other dogs and has happily shared kennels and enjoyed play dates with a variety of canine companions. She is respectful around toys and eats well alongside other dogs, making her an easy companion to have around.

She is now walking on a harness and has made lovely progress, although some things can still make her nervous when out and about. Her adopters will need to be patient and reassuring, helping her to feel safe and encouraging her when she encounters new experiences. She gains confidence from having another dog alongside her and would benefit from a calm canine friend to help her navigate the world.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life. She will need help with house training and learning the everyday routines that most pet dogs take for granted. She enjoys treats, so positive reinforcement will be a wonderful way to help her learn and build confidence. She will need a home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers 13+. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

Pushkin is a special little lady who has so much love to give. With plenty of patience, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, she will continue to blossom into a wonderful companion. She has brought so much joy to those caring for her, and we know that the lucky family who adopts her will absolutely adore her.

She has been treated for a ear infection.

Pushkin has been given the Gift of Life by Cherry Lewis

The last two weeks or so Pushkin, along with her kennel buddy Maggie, has been joining the big play group down the big play yard everyday (weather permitted) and she absolutely loves it. She enjoys saying hello to the other doggies there and play chases with some of them, it's so cute to watch, it makes my heart melt. It's amazing to see how much her confidence has grown, she really is blossoming.

She is quite attached to me, and does get excited to see me, she loves getting fusses from me, and is never too far from where I am if we're in a yard together, so if you like having a little extra shadow following you around she could be the girl for you.I took her out today on just a lead instead of a harness and she did amazingly, that being said for safety reasons and until she is comfortable and feels safe with you adopters would need to walk her on a harness for a while.Pushkin is just an amazing girl, I can't praise her enough and I'm always more than happy to talk about her with anyone who is interested in adopting her.

This beautiful lady brightens up my days, and as this has been a difficult week for me personally, she has been there to put a smile on my face through it.She can be nervous when you meet her initially but her confidence has grown so much she just needs time to warm up to you and figure you out, but once she's comfortable and her personality comes out she's just so much fun, and so loving. She has such a quirky personality and I absolutely adore her.Pushkin does walk on a harness, although some things do make her nervous still when out on a walk so adopters will need to be aware of this and let her know she is safe as well as some encouragement.Pushkin gets along with pretty much all dogs, any dog she has been kennelled with or introduced to for a play date she has always been so good, is fine with toys around and also eats well around the other dogs.She has never lived in a home before so her new family will have to show her the ropes and help her with her house training, be encouraging and use positive reinforcement, she does enjoy treats so they should be a big help.I'm not lying when I say I genuinely get excited to see her everyday I'm at work, she really is a little ray of sunshine.

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She is initially quite nervous and unsure, but once you spend some time with her she starts to come out of her shell and even begins to enjoy a fuss.

Pushkin is a sweet girl who simply needs understanding and the chance to build her confidence at her own pace. She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in gradually and continue to blossom. She takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes quite worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and show her that the world isn't such a frightening place.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She has made lovely progress with her harness training and is now walking on a harness, although she is still a little nervous when out and about. She is much more confident when she has another dog alongside her, so having a calm canine companion to help reassure her on walks will be a real benefit. She will need a home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

With plenty of love, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, Pushkin will continue to grow in confidence and become a wonderful companion. She is a lovely girl with so much potential, and we can't wait to see her enjoying the happy life she truly deserves.

name: Nora
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’m new to walking on a harness and doing well!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Nora is a gentle girl who has come to us from a breeder and is now in foster, where she has been able to experience life in a home for the first time. She has been in foster for over a month now, and this has given us a much better understanding of her mobility, as well as allowing her confidence to grow and her lovely personality to shine through.

Nora is still very mistrustful of people, but she is beginning to show us that she really does want to make friends. She is now much more willing to approach her fosterer and has recently started coming over to take treats from her. She will even jump up onto the sofa to watch Netflix, as long as there is another dog already on the sofa with her! These may seem like small things, but for Nora they are huge steps forward and show just how much she is beginning to relax. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her home that will allow her to lean on them as she continues to settle.

She absolutely loves the comforts of home life and takes great reassurance from having other dogs around her. She has also been on a few short walks outside the home, allowing her to slowly experience the world beyond her garden. She is still a very sensitive girl and everything will need to be introduced gradually, but she is making lovely progress.

Nora's mobility has also improved in a home setting. Her ataxia appears to be closely linked to her stress levels and is much more noticeable when she is worried or overwhelmed. When she is relaxed, her movements are almost normal, which is incredibly encouraging. She is not currently on any medication, and her fosterer is helping her to build muscle strength through daily massage and gentle exercise.

Nora will need a quiet and understanding home with adopters who have experience with nervous dogs and, ideally, ex-breeders. She will need at least one calm, friendly resident dog to give her confidence and show her the way. Her new family will need to be incredibly patient and allow her to settle and build trust at her own pace, without expecting too much too soon.

Nora has had lots of hardships in her life and is still learning that she can feel safe around people. However, the progress she has made since moving into foster has been wonderful to see. Beneath her worries is a very sweet girl who is slowly discovering how lovely life can be, and we are hoping that the right home will give her the security, patience and love she needs to continue blossoming.

Nora has been given the Gift of Life by Judie Fisher

Nora has been in foster for over a month now which allowed us to have a good assessment of her mobility, and also helped increase her confidence and introduce her to living in a home. This gentle girl has a very sweet personality and loves the comforts of home life and the company of other dogs. She is still very mistrustful of humans, but I can see that she is now more willing to try and be friends. She has recently started coming up to take a treat from me, and will even jump up on the sofa to watch Netflix with me (as long as there is another dog on the sofa too). She has also been on a few short walks outside to see the world beyond my home and garden!

Nora's ataxia has improved in a home setting too, largely because it is connected to her mental state and seems to be worse when she is stressed. When Nora is relaxed, her movements are almost normal, which is lovely to see and gives me hope that once she feels safe and comfortable mentally, she will have a great quality of life. We just need to help her get there. Nora is not on any medication at the moment, but I massage her daily and we are working on building her muscle strength.

Nora's ideal home will be a quiet setting with one or more calm and friendly dogs. Her people will need to be kind and very patient, with experience of scared dogs and preferably beagles too. This gorgeous girl has had lots of hardships in her life, it is time for her to finally have a place where she feels safe and loved.

I have been working with Nora a few days a week since she first arrived with us and was on medication and crate rest for her legs. Around two weeks ago, Nora moved to a different section, so I haven't seen her in a little while. I popped over today to check in and chat to one of her new kennel dads to see how she's doing.

Since arriving on her new section, Nora has made huge leaps! She is now harness-trained and wears her harness comfortably during the day. She has grown more confident with handling and with walking on her harness to and from the yard, though she is not yet feeling up to walks outside the centre. She also now sits curiously at the front of her kennel, watching people and dogs come and go on her section, rather than hiding in the back.

Nora still has a long way to go in learning to trust humans and receive our love, but she's made huge steps already. It's a great reminder that all of us working here have different skills, and sometimes a dog who is struggling just needs a change of scene to take the next steps in their journey towards their forever home.

Nora is so gentle and if you ignore the deep defensive howl (she is a beagle after all!) eventually she quietens down and she shows her soft side.Nora is still trying to get used to enjoying human company. She is not there yet but is slowly beginning to show signs of trusting people and does settle near you with a little patience.

It appears to me that it's not that Nora dislikes people, it's more a matter of how she is unsure of who we are and how we do things.

Once she  settles and it does take a little time, although still afraid, is much more willing to be approached by people.

In this calmer state, I was able to smooth her coat all over and gently stroke her without her worrying too much which is a positive step for her.

Nora will need this gentle approach for some time but the reward will be endless love and loyalty which is priceless.

I believe all Nora needs right now is the stability and security that a loving home can offer.Nora does much prefer the company of dogs  at the moment so it is a must that there is a resident dog already in the home for her to be with.

Nora has kennelled with small dogs but we do feel she would be better placed with a dog of a similar size or larger.

Our next step whilst Nora is with us will be to train her to walk on a harness so she can start to discover and enjoy the outside world.

Nora has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is a scared girl who is understandably feeling overwhelmed to find herself here and is desperately in need of kindness, patience and TLC as she begins to settle and learn that the world can be a safe place.

When Nora first arrived with us, she was showing some neurological symptoms and ataxia, and her back legs would occasionally slide from underneath her, causing her to stumble. Following investigations with our vets, it was found that her proprioception was delayed in all four limbs. She was trialed on a course of medication alongside crate rest and has made wonderful progress. Her proprioception is now normal, she is able to get around and play happily, and she enjoys life much more comfortably. She does still have a slight amount of ataxia and can occasionally limp still. Our vet feels that she may have suffered an acute injury at some point in the past which has largely resolved itself, though she will likely never present like a normal dog.

Nora will be looking for adopters who will love and cherish her just as she is. Due to her mobility history, she will need a home without slippery flooring, or one where plenty of rugs and runners are in place to help her move around confidently and safely.

She would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and understand her worries. Nora will need time to settle at her own pace and will thrive with patient adopters who are happy to let her progress in her own time. She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to show her the way and help her build confidence.

Nora has never experienced life in a home before so her new family will need to be understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and initially she will need to practise wearing her harness and exploring safely within the home and garden before she is ready to venture further afield.

Although Nora is still very worried and unsure of the world around her, beneath her fears is a sweet and deserving little girl who simply needs someone to believe in her. Watching a scared dog slowly learn to trust is one of the most rewarding experiences, and with love, patience and understanding, Nora will blossom. The day she greets you with a wagging tail and a sparkle in her eyes will make every moment of that journey worthwhile.

name: Nicole
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She was very scared when she first arrived and had clearly had little handling or socialisation, making human contact very worrying for her.

Nicole briefly moved into a foster home to learn about home life but returned to us following one incident where she became tangled in her lead and harness, panicked and nipped her fosterer. This was a single incident during a frightening experience, but adopters must understand that she can panic if she feels trapped or overwhelmed.

Nicole has now been back at the rescue for just over a month and is making lovely progress. She still doesn't like being picked up or handled, but is much better than she was and is increasingly comfortable spending time around people she trusts. She enjoys sitting in the play yard with her trusted people and responds brilliantly to treats, which are helping to build her confidence. She is a curious, cheeky little character who loves food, toys and snoozing in her bed, and she is even trying hard to be kennel clean.

Nicole loves other dogs and takes comfort from their presence, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog to help her feel secure and act as a role model.

She needs a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs. As she has never successfully experienced home life, she will need patience with house training and learning the basics of being a pet. Lead and harness training will also need to be introduced very carefully because of her previous experience.

Nicole still has a long way to go, but her curiosity and wonderful personality are beginning to shine through. With the right home, canine companion and plenty of time and understanding, we hope she will continue to blossom.

Our vets noted a slightly unusual heart rhythm, and a heart scan showed mild valve changes. She currently requires no treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although routine heart checks and monitoring for future symptoms are recommended. She has been treated for a ear infection.

Nicole has been given the Gift of Life by Shirley Bourne

Nicole has been back at the rescue with me for just over a month now, and even though she is still a scared lady, I can definitely see she has made progress. She still doesn’t like to be picked up and handled, but she’s a lot better with it now than she was when she first arrived. She’s also more content just being in my presence now and will happily hang out with me in the play yard with confidence. I spend a lot of time sitting on the floor with her and dishing out treats every so often to stay in her good books. She does love her food, so this helps massively with building some trust with her!

Nicole does still have a long way to go until she’s anywhere near being a ‘normal’ dog, but she has a lot of curiosity in her and definitely some Shih Tzu attitude as well, so I’m hoping she will blossom in the right home. If you have lots of time and patience, and a space in your heart and home to welcome a special lady, please consider Nicole. I promise you won’t regret it!

Nicole is the type of dog that can instantly put a smile on your face, even when she’s not doing anything. She has such a comical and infectious energy, and I really just love spending time with her. She loves snoozing in bed in her kennel through the day and playing with toys too. She even tries her hardest to be kennel clean!! She’s very easy to look after day to day. So please… give her a chance.

Nicole has been in foster for a week and is a sweetie. She has a wonderfully inquisitive nature and loves investigating everything around her, which makes us chuckle! She is still very nervous about being handled and will bark when she's feeling unsure, but she is already making progress. She now takes treats from us and absolutely loves her food. She is also mostly clean overnight.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She is a lovely little girl who is understandably feeling very scared and overwhelmed to find herself here. It’s clear she hasn’t had much handling or socialisation before, so human hands are quite worrying for her at the moment, but we will continue gently helping her learn that hands can be kind.

Nicole will be looking for a calm and quiet adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would really benefit from adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience, time and reassurance she will need as she learns to trust.

She loves other dogs and takes great comfort from their presence, so Nicole will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure.

As Nicole has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who are ready to help her learn everything about home life from the very beginning. She will need to learn new skills like house training and will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness.

With time, kindness and plenty of TLC, Nicole will begin to grow in confidence and let her personality shine.

Our vets have noted that Nicole has a slightly unusual heart rhythm, so she underwent a heart scan at our vets which showed some mild valve changes. At this stage she does not require any treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although we would recommend routine heart checks and monitoring for any future symptoms.

name: Dutch
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and muzzle trained. I would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is muzzle trained and wears a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

I still can’t quite understand how this incredibly smart and loving boy hasn’t found his forever home yet.If you’re looking for a dog to train, learn new tricks and go on lots of adventures with, then Dutch really is your boy.He’s the best of both worlds a crazy, energetic boy who also absolutely loves his people and loves nothing more than a good snuggle.

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.
