As you would expect from a Fox Hound, Todd is high-energy and needs a very active home that can provide him with plenty of daily exercise.  Walks alone may not be enough to keep his body and mind satisfied, so he would really benefit from additional activities such as scent work, tracking games, enrichment and other opportunities to use his wonderful Hound brain.  Todd is also a vocal boy – hounds are known for their voices, and Todd is certainly not shy about using his!  His new family will need to appreciate that hound singing, baying and general commentary are part of the package.  Hounds are also known for being escape artists so he will need secure, hound-proof fencing and careful management, particularly when he is outdoors. A home that understands the determination and curiosity of a scent-driven hound would be ideal.  Todd has so much character and has all the makings of a fantastic companion in the right home.  He needs someone who understands that a Fox Hound is a lifestyle, not just a pet – but for the right home, Todd will bring plenty of fun, affection and adventure.

Todd has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care and is very playful and full-on.  We do feel he could potentially live with another dog of similar energy levels that would tolerate his play style following a successful meet and greet.

As Todd came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Shadow
description:
Shadow is a very affectionate boy who has been super friendly to our staff and volunteers since he came in to our care. With him being an ex racer, he does have a high prey drive so can try to chase squirrels whilst out for his walks! He absolutely loves chasing his toys around our secure compound.  He is a really affectionate boy who loves lots of fuss and attention.

Shadow will have spent most of his life in kennels with his racing background, so he may feel a little nervous going in to a home environment. We also do not know if he is house trained or toilet trained due to this. He loves to lie in his comfy beds after his walks – we sometimes catch him upside down showing his belly off!

Shadow has now been in our care for 237 days and is desperately searching for his forever home.

We think Shadow would prefer to be the only dog in the home as he can sometimes be a little unsure around them and isn’t too interested in interacting with them.

He could also potentially live with children 14+ years  – subject to a successful meet.

Shadow would love a home where he could relax and enjoy his retirement years and rest on a comfy bed (or couch) of his own!

name: Oscar
description:
Meet Oscar! He is a lovely boy with a huge personality and plenty of puppyish energy!  Oscar is a very lively, energetic and friendly boy who is always ready for his next adventure.  He is a big puppy at heart – giddy, playful and full of enthusiasm and he loves being around people.  Oscar can be quite an excitable boy and does jump up, particularly when he is happy or excited.  He is also very vocal, so his new family should be prepared for a dog who likes to make his presence known!  Oscar has a very playful side.  When staff are cleaning his kennel, he thinks the hose pipe and brushes are fantastic toys and will chase them around.  His enthusiasm can sometimes get the better of him, so he will need patient guidance to learn more appropriate ways to channel his energy.  On walks, Oscar does pull on the lead and will need continued training to help him develop his loose-lead walking skills.  He would really benefit from an owner who enjoys training and can provide consistent positive reinforcement.  Oscar is looking for an active home where he can enjoy plenty of exercise, enrichment and mental stimulation.  He is not a couch-potato kind of boy!  His ideal family will enjoy getting out and about with him and be prepared to give him the time and training he needs to mature into a well-mannered adult.  His new adopter should be willing to work on his impulse control, socialisation and general training.  As a young Lurcher, Oscar will need patience, consistency and plenty of appropriate outlets for his energy.  Underneath all that excitement is a loveable, friendly and very giddy young boy who is still learning about the world.  He will need a private secure garden.

Oscar has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care and is very playful.  We do feel he could potentially be rehomed with another lively and energetic dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Oscar came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Hero
description:
Hero is an ex racing greyhound who is now looking for his forever home with a family that can help him settle into life beyond the kennels. He is a confident, lively boy with plenty of personality. He gets very excited when it’s time for a walk and can jump around on the lead, so will need someone who is comfortable handling a tall strong greyhound. With a little training and consistency this is something that can be worked on. Although he is confident in many ways, he does need help building his confidence when it comes to being touched and handled as he can get a little worried.  Hero deserves the chance to learn, grow and discover just how good life can be outside of kennels.

Hero can be rehomed with mature children who are 16 years and over, due to his size and bouncy nature. This will be subject to a successful meet.

Hero is currently paired with another greyhound and has interreacted well with dogs whilst in our care, so we believe that he would be rehomed with another dog- subject to a successful meet and greet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Mischief
description:
Meet Mischief!  This lovely girl is looking for a very special home.  Mischief is a very timid and nervous girl who has slowly started to come out of her shell.  She will need patient, understanding adopters who are willing to give her the time and space she needs to build confidence and learn that she is safe.  Once Mischief trusts you, you get to see the sweet girl underneath.  She is affectionate and loving, enjoys giving kisses, and absolutely loves a good belly rub.  Seeing her begin to relax and show her gentle personality is incredibly rewarding.  Mischief does have a cheeky side to her name!  She is a talented escape artist and has been known to jump the kennel walls, so her new home will need secure fencing and adopters who are prepared for her Houdini tendencies.  Extra care will be needed to make sure the doesn’t escape open doors or fences.  Mischief is not looking for a busy or rushed home.  She needs someone who understands that trust takes time and is willing to let her progress at her own pace.  Any potential adopters will need to commit to several regular meet and greets before the adoption can take place.

Mischief has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, although she does prefer a calmer dog.  We do feel she could be rehomed with another calm dog following a successful meet and greet (must be neutered).

As Mischief came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her and as she can be very nervous we would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Bear
description:
Bear is a very nervous boy when he meets new people for the first time. It takes a little while for him to come around but with patience and yummy treats he slowly starts to trust you. Once he has gained your trust and is comfortable he is an affectionate boy and loves to give out kisses. He will need to have multiple regular meets before going home.

Bear is a big dog who doesn’t understand his size, he is constantly jumping up for cuddles and doesn’t know what personal space is. Bear is going to require a lot of training to help him learn manners. He can be a very cheeky boy at times! He will need socialising in different environments and around people to help him build his confidence up. Bear gets super excited when going for walks and is very strong on the lead, this is another area that will need more training. Bear loves playing with his toys, splashing around in water and zooming around our enclosed area.

Bear is after an adult only home that has previous experience with big boisterous dogs. No regular visiting children either please. He is going to need a very active home with a family that is able to provide him with plenty of exercise and mental stimulation to keep him busy. As he is still only a young dog he can get up to mischief when he is bored. Bear’s new family need to be committed to putting in the training that he needs not only initially but keeping it up for the rest of his life.

Bear needs to be the only dog in the home so that he can have all of attention to help get him settled. Bear can interact well with dogs whilst out on walks but will need further training to help improve this.

We know that Bear is going to require a lot of work at first but once he is trained he will make a lovely family dog who will love going on plenty of adventures. Taking on a dog this size is a big commitment, please ensure that you are serious and have thought about the future before applying.

name: Ripley
description:
Meet Ripley!! He is a gorgeous boy looking for an active, committed home where he can continue to learn and thrive.  He’s a friendly, affectionate boy with a fun-loving personality and is always ready for a game with his favourite toys.  He is full of energy and loves to play, so he will need an active family who can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and ongoing training.  Like many young dogs, he can become a little mouthy and nippy when he’s excited, so he will benefit from patient guidance and positive reinforcement to help him learn appropriate manners.  He is still working on his basic commands and will need someone willing to continue his training.  He can also occasionally rag his lead, so further lead training will be important.  Previous experience with Shar-pei’s would be a real advantage, as they can have their own unique characteristics and training needs.  He currently has a cherry eye, which will be surgically repaired before he goes to his new home, so he’ll be ready to start his next chapter feeling his best.  If you’re looking for a playful, lively young dog and have to time and commitment to help him become the wonderful companion we know he can be, Ripley could be the boy for you.

Ripley has socialised well with other dogs and is very playful with them.  He can sometimes get frustrated and bark if he can’t get to them straight away.  We feel he could potentially be rehomed with another playful dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Ripley came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him and as he can be a little nippy when over-excited we would like any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Salem
description:
Meet Salem!  She is looking for an active and understanding home where she can really thrive.  Salem can be nervous and unsure around new people but once she has built that trust, her sweet personality begins to shine through.  Being a typical Terrier, Salem is full of energy and enthusiasm! she loves getting out for long walks and would be a fantastic companion for someone who enjoys plenty of outdoor adventures. She will need a very active home that can provide her with lots of daily exercise as well as plenty of mental stimulation to keep her busy and happy.  Salem absolutely loves toys and enjoys having something to play with and keep her occupied.  She can, however, be quite the toy destroyer when she gets bored, so enrichment and appropriate things to chew will be important for her.  Salem can be vocal while in her kennel, particularly when she is excited, frustrated or looking for attention.  She would benefit from owners who understand Terrier traits and are happy to continue training and socialisation with her.  She will need a private secure garden.

Salem was previously rehomed but has since been returned to our care following an incident involving another dog.  She can get along with some dogs but her previous owner said she wasn’t compatible with all dogs, so her interactions need to be carefully managed.  Her new owner will need to be understanding of her individual needs and committed to working with her through gradual, controlled introductions and ongoing training to help her feel comfortable around other dogs.  She will need an owner who is willing to take things at her pace.

As Salem came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Elias
description:
Elias is a very sweet and friendly boy. He came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on him. He has always been friendly with staff and volunteers whilst here. Elias can be a little strong on the lead due to his size so some basic lead training would be beneficial for him. We are looking for an active home for Elias as he has a lot of energy and would enjoy going on lots of adventures. Elias is a calm boy in his kennel and loves to have some down time with a tasty chew.

Elias is a friendly boy but due to his size we believe that it would be best for him to be rehomed with children over 14 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

Elias needs a little more training around dogs since his castration as he has become a little unsure, therefore we believe that Elias would benefit from being the only dog in the home as he would prefer all the attention on him.

name: Jasper
description:
Jasper is an ex-racing greyhound that has spent all of his life in kennels. Jasper is now ready for a comfortable and cosy forever home to call his own. Jasper is a friendly and loveable boy who likes attention and a cuddle. Jasper has a high prey drive still so does pull when he sees ducks, birds and wildlife when out on walks. Jasper has never lived in a home before so he will need time to settle and get used to unfamiliar sounds and objects.

Jasper has interacted well with dogs and is currently paired with another greyhound so we believe that he can be rehomed with another dog of a similar size – Subject to a successful meet.

Jasper is a sweet boy so can potentially be rehomed with children who are 12 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

name: Sam
description:
Sam is a very loveable boy who just wants to give out hugs to everyone he meets, he does sometimes forget how big he is though. He’s a big hit with volunteers here and they all love taking him out for his walks as they get to have lots of cuddles. He can be strong on the lead though due to his size. He’s a very sweet boy who has a big heart and is looking for someone to show him lots of love! Sam has enjoyed his walks around the woods, watching the ducks and wildlife around him. Sam would appreciate an enclosed garden that he can spend his time in relaxing and enjoying the sun. Sam loves his treats, nothing is too big or small for him – he isn’t fussy!

Sam is super friendly with everyone he meets but due to his giddy jumpy nature we believe that it would be best to rehome Sam with children over the age of 16 – subject to a successful meet and greet.

Sam needs to be the only dog in the home, he can be vocal around dogs so needs a family that has experience to help build his confidence and manners.

If you think that you could provide a comfortable home with lots of treats for Sam please apply now!

name: Cali
description:
Cali was a very nervous girl when she first arrived at the home, which was over 200 days now! It has taken a lot of time for staff and volunteers to get to know Cali and bring out her excitable, bubbly personality. Cali loves going for walks and off lead runs in our compound area, she will always be found with a football in her mouth. She loves to dodge past you whilst you try and catch her, her tail never stops wagging. Cali loves her treats and sits nicely whilst you give them to her. She has been toilet trained whilst in our care, which is a bonus for when she goes home.

Cali can be strong on the lead at times due to her excitement to get outside and enjoy the fresh air but can walk nicely after her initial excitement is over, especially on a harness. Cali would love a fully enclosed garden with someone around most of the time so that she can come and go as she pleases. Cali spends most of her day relaxing on a comfy bed watching people come and go. She can be a little barky in her kennel at first but this is due to her wanting to say hello to everyone.

Cali isn’t a cuddly kind of girl but would love a family that is willing to keep her entertained and will play with her toys. We believe that Cali needs to be in an adult only home, with a family that has experience with rescue dogs or bull breeds.

Cali was nervous of dogs when she first came into our care so we think that it is best that she is the only dog in the house. With a lot of socialisation she now is a friendly girl that is happy to say hello to most dogs that she meets.

We think that it would be best for Cali to not be in a house with cats.

If you think you can give this gorgeous girl her forever home please apply!

name: Pearl
description:
This talkative girl is Pearl.  She is a very affectionate, confident and friendly girl that is always up for lots of fuss and strokes.  She can be very vocal when she wants your attention so probably not suitable for an apartment/flat.  She enjoys her walks everyday having a sniff about and saying hello to everyone she meets.  She is very strong on the lead so will need an experienced owner that is used to powerful dogs. Pearl would benefit from a private secure garden.

Pearl has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, she can be a little unsure at first but does come around after a bit, so we feel she may be best suited as the only dog in the home where she can take her time getting used to other dogs with lots of positive reinforcement from her new adopter.

As Pearl came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 12+ years.

name: Nala
description:
Nala is a 4 year old female Cross-Breed, D.O.B. 14/09/2021, who was rescued in Romania in September 2024 along with her 9 puppies. She is a sweet, gentle dog who is still learning to trust people.

She is naturally cautious and nervous around new people but is gradually opening up to her foster and showing her true nature.

Nala would benefit from a calm, quiet environment to help her feel safe and take things at her own pace. Ideally, she needs to live with another calm, confident resident dog or dogs who can help her gain trust in her surroundings.

Nala weighs approximately 20kg and stands 50cm tall from floor to withers. She is spayed, fully vaccinated, and enjoys the company of other dogs. She takes no notice of cats. Due to Nala’s shyness, we recommend a home without children.

Nala can be left for a few hours as long as she has the company of other dogs. She is happy to sleep downstairs in her basket at night.

Nala is currently in Cullompton, Devon. However, transport can be arranged for the right adopter.

Stray2Me is a UK registered charity (No. 1186687), with trustees and volunteers across the country.

Home check and adoption donation apply. Full rescue backup and support provided.

name: Balto
description:
Little Balto was abandoned and was living the life of strays in a village with his two siblings when he was rescued.

Sadly their beautiful mum is still out there, too frightened of people to be caught.

At just 4 months old, Balto is a sweet-natured little boy with a beautiful, smiling face and a heart to match. He’s soft, cuddly and friendly with everyone he meets.

He is playful and kind, loves other dogs and would be delighted to have a canine friend in his new home. He could also live with older, dog savvy children.

Balto is expected to be medium size when fully grown and is ready to travel to his new home once the right family is found for him.

He has his whole life ahead of him and he’s ready to start a new chapter — one filled with love, safety and cuddles.

name: Mocca
description:
I’m not the shyest dog you’ll meet, but right now… I am a very confused one.

When I was just a tiny puppy, I was found in Romania with my brother and sister. We didn’t have much—no warm beds, no full bowls, just each other. Then we were taken to a shelter.

That’s where the older, wiser dogs told us stories… stories about a magical place far away where dogs had families. Real families.

They said dogs slept in warm beds, never went hungry, and went on adventures—sniffing grass, chasing leaves, even watching squirrels.

They said you needed a “golden ticket” to get there. And somehow… we got one.

We came to the UK. And for a little while, I thought the stories were true. I had a home. I had people. I had hope.

But then… after just a few weeks… they decided they didn’t want me anymore.

They said I guarded my food and toys. And maybe I did. When you grow up with nothing, it’s hard to understand that things won’t be taken away. I held on too tightly… because I was scared of losing everything again.

The girls here are helping me every day, and I’m getting better. I’m starting to understand that food comes back, toys come back… that I don’t have to be afraid anymore.

I absolutely love humans. I’ve had some good training, I can walk nicely on the lead, and I’m good with other dogs too.

Every time a volunteer walks past my kennel, I get so excited. I think, “This is it. I’m going home.” But I always have to come back… and it breaks my heart a little more each time.

So I’m asking—please. Share my story far and wide. Someone out there must have space for me. I don’t need perfect… I just need a chance.

name: Lika
description:
Lika is a deaf young dog whose foster family writes , she is one of the sweetest-natured dogs they have ever met. She is full of life, always looking for her next adventure, and brings a constant sense of fun wherever she goes.

She is a happy, confident pup with no signs of trauma. Lika approaches the world with complete trust and enthusiasm and absolutely adores people. She gives the most wonderful cuddles and thrives on affection.

Because she is deaf, Lika doesn’t always pick up on signals from other dogs, and her play style can be very boisterous. She loves other dogs, but her unfiltered excitement can overwhelm them, especially smaller or more sensitive dogs.

She is responding well to hand signals and already knows some basic commands. Like any puppy, she can be selective at times, but she is very food-motivated, which makes training enjoyable and rewarding.

“Sit” for a treat is already spot on! Lika would suit an active home that enjoys the outdoors and can offer: Plenty of exercise Ongoing training using positive, reward-based methods. Mental stimulation and engagement.

Although it may sound surprising given her deafness, we feel that with a dedicated handler she could even enjoy activities like agility, where visual communication is key.

She is not destructive, but she does love to carry things around and enjoys her toys and chew bones. Lika has not been tested with cats.

We feel Lika would be happiest: As the only dog, or with a confident, well-balanced dog who can clearly set boundaries She would particularly suit someone with experience of high-energy breeds such as Border Collies.

Lika was found abandoned in the countryside with her 5 siblings and her mother. A friend of our volunteer asked for our help. A vet took 5 of the siblings and they are now in a private shelter. We took Lika. As yet, we have been unable to secure the mother.

name: Duchess
description:
Meet Duchess our 4 ½ year old, Female, German Shepherd Cross. Unfortunately we have not had any enquires for Duchess as yet, which we simply can’t understand why.

Duchess came to us in a state of neglect, she was very thin, and had what looked like untreated sores. Through the dedication of our team she is now a much happier healthier dog.

This loving smiley dog, loves attention, and will give plenty in return. She loves her toys, and once she has found her favourite one she will carry it with her everywhere.

She is an active dog, and would suit a home that has a similar lifestyle. She loves to go for a walk, and have play. She walks ok on the lead, she can be a bit excitable to start with, but soon settles down once she has her toy to hold.

She would suit a home where she is the only animal, but could settle well in a home with older children.

name: Vera
description:
Meet Vera, our very smiley 2-year-old female Staffordshire Bull Terrier cross.

She loves to meet new people and will quite happily take any affection you can give her. She has a lot of love to give.

She walks well on the lead and will happily sit for treats. She does like to be kept active and would enjoy going out for walks with you.

We would recommend that Vera be the only animal in the home, but could settle well into a home with older children.

name: Lola, Lena, Luna and Lyra
description:
Lola, Lena, Luna and Lyra – looking for homes

Meet Luna, Lola, Lena & Lyra – Four Little Cuddle Monsters Looking for Love!

Size: Expected to be medium-sized, although their parentage is unknown

These four gorgeous girls have already had a rather tough start to life. Found abandoned between a road and a river, and without their mum, they were taken into the care of the shelter we work with.

Thankfully, their story is now taking a much happier turn, and they are ready to find families of their very own!

So, what are they like? Simply delightful! Luna, Lola, Lena and Lyra have been an absolute joy. They have been lovely with everyone they have met, including people, children and other dogs.

They are affectionate, sociable little girls who seem to love everyone and are very happy to make new friends. If you are looking for a puppy who enjoys cuddles, these girls certainly fit the bill – they are real little cuddle monsters!

They have also been surprisingly good in their kennels.

They are not destructive and have been so grateful for their blankets and comfy bedding.

Even during a storm, they coped brilliantly, showing just how lovely and adaptable these little characters can be.

These girls could suit a variety of homes, with or without another dog.

They have been great with children, so sensible, dog-aware children should be absolutely fine, provided introductions and interactions are always managed appropriately.

They have not been cat-tested, but we feel they may be able to live with cats in the right circumstances, with careful, gradual introductions and appropriate supervision.

As with any young puppy, they will need a family who has the time and patience to help them learn all about life in a home.

Toilet training is still a work in progress, although they have done very well during their time with us.

They will also need to learn about walking nicely on a lead, alongside all the other important lessons that come with growing up.

Ideally a home with a secure garden will allow them a safe space to work on their training.

We expect them to grow into lovely medium-sized dogs, but as we do not know their parentage, we cannot guarantee their adult size.

A note about their veterinary care Luna, Lola, Lena and Lyra are currently around four months old. They are not yet spayed because they are too young, so spaying will be a requirement of their adoption contract once they are old enough.

Could one of these lovely girls be the missing piece of your family?

They have already shown themselves to be affectionate, friendly and wonderfully good-natured puppies. Now they need families who will continue to help them grow, learn and discover all the wonderful things life has to offer.

If you think you could offer Luna, Lola, Lena or Lyra the loving home they deserve, please visit www.savingandrehomingstrays.org to find out more about our adoption process.

All four puppies are at our rescue in Ayr and are ready for their new homes. Adopters must be able to travel to Ayr for a meet and greet and collection.

A home check and adoption donation apply. Their new families must also be happy to fulfil the spaying requirement in their adoption contract. Please help us find these four little cuddle monsters the wonderful futures they deserve!

name: Ayaz
description:
Ayaz, 5 years old medium size cross breed male.

Ayaz is one of the 27 dogs rescued from a hoarding case back in October, a group of dogs who had never known normal life, kindness, or what it means to feel safe.

He is a gentle, sensitive boy who has already made lovely progress. Ayaz walks nicely on a lead and really enjoys getting out, often getting excited when it’s time to go for a walk.

It’s a big step for a dog with his past, and he’s embracing it more and more.

He finds comfort in other dogs and will need a home with a confident canine companion to help him feel safe and continue learning about the world.

Ayaz is still unsure when it comes to human affection. He’s not quite ready for cuddles yet and prefers to keep a little distance, but we can see the soft, trusting boy underneath.

With time, patience, and a calm environment, he will get there.

Ayaz will need a quiet home with understanding adopters who won’t rush him. A home where he can build confidence at his own pace and continue to blossom.

He may not be the dog who runs into your arms right away… but with the right family, Ayaz has everything it takes to become a truly special companion

name: Billy
description:
Our extra special boy Billy is approximately three years old and an intriguing cross breed at the very bottom end of medium.

Billy weighs twelve kilos and measures ten inches from shoulder to paw. Having been found abandoned on the streets Billy has been in our Cyprus shelter for two months.

Billy is described by our shelter manager as rather shy and enjoys a very sweet nature and is especially calm. He has a happy and jolly disposition and so enjoys his time with people.

Billy’s appearance is exceptional. His largely black torso is beautifully enhanced with a white flash to his snout along with five white tips and his chest and tummy.

Billy is a truly exceptional adoption candidate who will prove a loyal and loving companion to his forever family. Such an affable and charming little chap.

Billy enjoys his time in the car and walks nicely on his lead. He seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Bertie
description:
Our extra special boy Bertie is approximately seven years old and a medium sized hound of sorts. Bertie weighs sixteen kilos and measures fourteen inches from shoulder to paw.

Very sadly Bertie has been in our Cyprus shelter since he was two having been abandoned on the streets.

Our shelter manager describes Bertie perfectly. He has a wonderful calm personality, a little timid and would make a fabulous companion.

Having spent so much of his life waiting patiently it is now time and in fact long overdue for Bertie to secure his forever home.

Everything is correct about Bertie but for being so meek, mild and well behaved he has simply been overlooked. Such a good-looking handsome boy.

Bertie is the epitome of gentility and kindness. His adopters will be truly blessed and greatly rewarded.

Bertie enjoys his time in the car and walks nicely on the lead. He seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Rosie
description:
Our extra special girl Rosie is approximately three years old and an adorable cross breed at the very bottom of medium size.

Rosie weighs just ten kilos and measures eleven inches from shoulder to paw. Having been found abandoned on the streets Rosie has been in our Cyprus shelter for two months.

Our shelter manager describes Rosie as exceptionally well mannered. She has a wonderful bouncy personality and lights up the room. Equally she is calm and loves a cuddle.

Rosie has a unique charisma about her which makes her instantly attractive. Really the star of any show. Her appearance is sublime with her easy to manage solid black coat and subtle white flash to her chest.

If ever there was a readymade adoption candidate it’s Rosie. She is ready to fit into her forever home and donate years of happiness and gratitude to her fortunate adopters.

Rosie walks nicely on her lead and seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Obi
description:
Obi is a 5 year old male Chihuahua Cross.

Obi is a sensitive worried boy who will be looking for a kind patient home to build his confidence.

He is a fun active boy who loves his walks and playing and will looking for a new home who can match his energy levels.

Obi is looking for a calm quiet patient home where adopters will give him the space to bond and trust. He would like access to his own secure garden to help with confidence building.

He is housetrained, ok travelling, and may prefer a home with company. Obi can be worried by lots of noise and activity so would prefer a quiet home in a quiet area.

Obi can be worried when meeting new people and will require a calm quiet patient approach to making friends.

He will bond closely with those he trusts and becomes a cheeky affectionate boy! Obi may prefer an adult only home or a home where any children are older teenagers who would be happy to take a slow approach with him.

He may prefer a home with no young visiting children.

Obi has previously lived with other small dogs and has previously been described as social with other dogs. Obi can be worried by bigger dogs but is social with small dogs.

He may prefer to be the only dog in the home but could potentially live with a small confident female dog

Not suited to living with cats, birds or small animals as will chase.

Obi would like a home with an understanding of, and the time to, support him both behaviourally and emotionally. A home that understands he will need a gentle approach when making new friends.

Obi will require several meets to get to know someone.

name: Vroula
description:
Vroula is one of the 27 dogs rescued from a hoarding case back in October, and her story is one of quiet progress and gentle bravery.

She is still a very shy girl, but slowly, step by step, she is learning that the world doesn’t have to be so scary. Handling her has become much easier, and although she still keeps her distance in the playground, we are starting to see little flashes of curiosity.

Every now and then, she will come a bit closer for a treat or even allow a gentle cuddle from the children — small moments that feel huge for a dog like Vroula.

She is more wary of men than women and will need time to build trust, patience truly is key with her.

She is not yet walking on a lead, so she currently needs to be carried, but even here we see improvement as she becomes more comfortable with each passing week.

Vroula will need a calm, quiet home with patient adopters who understand that trust cannot be rushed. A home without too much pressure, where she can go at her own pace and continue building confidence.

Another calm, confident dog could really help show her the way.

She may not be the dog who runs straight into your arms on day one… but with time, kindness, and love, Vroula will get there. And when she does, it will be something very special.

name: Ron
description:
Ron is a four year old male Brittany. Ron is a very handsome boy. Small in size with a robust frame and vibrant colours.Ron is exceptionally attached to people.

He would like to spend all day by your side! He loves cuddles and caresses and has a very good appetite too whihc will be great for training!

Ron is very sociable with female dogs and but a little wary of other males, he will soon be neutered and we will see if he settles down more then.

He is a very active dog, he loves to be out in the enclosure having a run.

Ron was handed in to the shelter we work closely with in North Spain by his hunter. Ron is one of the many unwanted Spanish gun dogs.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Ron a home, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Ron is in Spain and ready to travel to his forever home in the UK.

name: Snickers
description:
Meet Snickers a medium size labrador cross boy.

Snickers’ story is one of those that stays with you. He and his siblings were found in the middle of a busy highway… tiny 4-month-old puppies left to survive the unthinkable.

Sadly, not all of them made it — some were hit by cars, and one disappeared and was never found.

Four of them were rescued. Snickers was one of the lucky ones.

His siblings — Bueno, Mars, and Bounty — didn’t wait long before finding their forever homes. But Snickers is still here… still waiting.

He was always the shyest of the four, and while his journey has been slower, it has also been incredibly special to watch. Over the past 15 months, Snickers has made beautiful progress.

He now gets excited when he sees us, eagerly waiting for his lead so he can go out to the playground — his favourite place, especially when there are treats involved.

Snickers is still a sensitive boy. While he will allow touch, he doesn’t fully enjoy cuddles just yet — but that’s simply part of his journey. He is learning, growing, and gaining confidence every day.

He is great with other dogs and would benefit from a calm, understanding home that will continue to build his confidence at his own pace.

A family who sees beyond the shyness, and understands that trust takes time, will be the perfect match for him.

Snickers may not run straight into your arms… but once he lets you into his world, it will be something truly special.

After everything he has been through, he deserves his chance.

name: Takis
description:
Meet Takis a small size beagle cross boy.

Takis is around 4 years old and a true survivor. He was rescued during the devastating wildfires last July, but his story started long before that.

Most likely abandoned as a puppy, Takis grew up alone in the mountains, learning to survive the only way he could.

Food was never guaranteed — he relied on a small local tavern that only opened on weekends, and the occasional kindness of visitors staying in nearby holiday homes. It was a fragile existence, but it was all he knew.

The villages were destroyed, the land was left burnt and empty… and somehow, Takis survived. But survival wasn’t enough anymore. The tavern stopped opening, the visitors stopped coming, and suddenly there was nothing left for him.

Takis was so shy he wouldn’t let anyone come closer than a metre. It took patience, planning, and four weeks of effort — but eventually, we managed to trap him and bring him to safety.

He was diagnosed with leishmania. Thankfully, his organs were not affected, and after completing his treatment, he is now doing really well.

Today, Takis is still a shy and sensitive boy, but he has come such a long way. He enjoys being outside, walks nicely on a lead, and is even starting to play with other dogs — something we could have never imagined before.

Takis is looking for a very special home. A calm, quiet environment with people who understand that love doesn’t always look like cuddles at first.

He will need patience, kindness, and the freedom to build trust at his own pace — even if that means loving him from a little distance in the beginning.

Because one day, that distance will close.

And when it does, it will be something truly special.

Takis has survived everything life has thrown at him. Now he deserves more than survival — he deserves a home, safety, and love for the rest of his life.

No dog should spend their life in a shelter…especially not one like Takis

name: Mason
description:
Mason is a medium sized crossbreed, he looks like he could be Labrador amongst other things. He is believed to be around seven to eight years old. Mason fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Mason has joined us recently from the Botosani public shelter in Romania where he and his father and siblings spent some years. Harvey and Mason are the last of the family to come to us here.

Mason has taken to domestic life far quicker than we expected. We are already being treated to tail wags and he’s approaching for fuss.

In the weeks ahead he will continue to grow in confidence but is already enjoying his new world away from his cell in the shelter. He would like another dog for company in his forever home and could live with respectful aged twelve plus.

name: Ducessa
description:
Ducessa is a medium to large shepherd cross-breed around 4 years old (Born in 2022).

Our beautiful ‘Duchess’, born 2022 and 24kg, is affectionate, sensitive and bonds very strongly with her people. If you enjoy the rewards of training a dog (especially Shepherd types) but are looking for a slightly smaller dog, Ducessa may be your girl.

Ducessa is partially sighted – she can see well enough but her fosterer thinks she has tunnel vision.

We are looking for a reasonably experienced home for Ducessa; ideally one with Shepherd or larger breed experience.

The right home will find the prospect of investing time into training part of her appeal. Ducessa is a work in progress but, as her foster carer says, after a few months she will be a cracking dog!

Ducessa is already brilliant in the house; she loves to curl up on the sofa with you, will even try to share your chair! She walks ‘like a dream’ on the lead; (‘one of the best dogs I’ve ever had on the lead’ says a very experienced fosterer!)

Ducessa prefers being close to her person than bounding around, and is easy to manage. She travels well, is crate trained and sleeps through the night, enjoying a lazy morning.

She’s not a greedy girl; prefers her walk before eating her breakfast. Although she does like her treats…this makes her easy to train.

Ducessa is still a nervous dog in many respects. Outside, on walks and in the garden, she barks. She barks at dogs, unusual noises, traffic and people she does not know.

Her body language shows fear and frustration – she isn’t wishing to be aggressive, but is unsure, needs reassurance, input from her owner.

Her tail never stops wagging; she does want to be involved; wants to play. Her new home will understand these behaviours and how to work with Ducessa to improve her confidence.

Ducessa needs slow introductions to dogs and people.

Strangers coming to the home will unsettle Ducessa initially, this is an area of training that is being addressed, but again, we will need someone with the patience and experience to help her gain confidence.

Prospective adopters would need to meet her several times before taking her home.

Introductions to any other dogs in the house would need to be done slowly, and adopters must have the ability to separate her whilst she gets used to new surroundings and other dogs in the house. Ducessa has now settled with the other 3 dogs in her foster home.

It is thought Ducessa is good with cats but has not been cat tested in the UK

Originally rescued from the streets of Romania, Ducessa is very submissive to people she knows (happy to have food removed, feet wiped etc), but lacks confidence in the world.

She is looking for someone or people who will enjoy giving her the right care in order for her to blossom.

Please note – we do not rehome dogs to families with children under the age of 10.

Adult home with some experience of rescue dogs, willing to put the time into making Ducessa feel safe and confident. A home which wants to carry on and enjoys training. Shepherd or larger breed experience would be useful.

Ducessa can live with another dog, but this dog must be calm, patient and kind, and dog savvy, and introductions must be done slowly with the separation options mentioned above.

We are told Ducessa previously was fine with cats (in Romania)

Ducessa needs a quietish household; not busy. Probably somewhere rural or semi rural. Ducessa’s adopters will be willing to travel to meet her several times in her foster home in Norfolk to meet her before collecting her.

Ducessa would love a home with a garden. She is looking for a home where people are around most of the time, as loves to be with people.

Please read about our Adoption process. We really appreciate it when potential adopters have read our advice, and these are the people who are most often successful at application stage! https://www.bdruk.org/rehome

Our adoption donation is £325. This includes travel to the UK, their vaccinations, pet passport, microchip and all preparation for travel. They also come with 5 weeks free insurance.

name: Bonnie
description:
Meet Beautiful Bonnie: Your Future Professional Snooze Supervisor!

Bonnie joined us as an unclaimed stray from the pound, she was in a horrific condition full of lumps and a mouth full of rotten teeth, she also suffers from dry eye.

She has been bred from a lot and had an umbilical hernia that was fixed when she was speyed. It seems a classic case of, she has made them all the money but now she is worthless to them so she was thrown out like rubbish.

Bonnies Microchip says she is 12 years old but we all find this so hard to believe, we would have put her around 6 years old if it wasn’t for the microchip. It just makes it even sadder nobody cared for her in her advancing years.

Hello there! I’m Bonnie, a mature English Bulldog looking for a cosy retirement spot.

If you are looking for a gentle, easy-going companion to bring instant warmth and character into your home, I am ready to fill that position!

At 12 years old, I have officially mastered the art of peaceful living. I’ve left all the puppy chaos far behind and am completely dedicated to the finer things in life: comfortable naps, gentle head scratches, and being your most loyal shadow.

The Companion Life: I give the gentlest affection and will happily sit right at your feet keeping you company while you read, work, or watch TV.

Life in the Slow Lane: My energy level is highly efficient! A very short, leisurely stroll to sniff the grass is plenty of exercise for me.

The rest of my day is strictly reserved for lounging.

Classic Bulldog Charm: I come with the full package of adorable bulldog wrinkles, a wiggly tail when I see you, and a soundtrack of soft, happy grunts and content snores that are guaranteed to make you smile every day.

Low-Maintenance Roommate: I am incredibly well-mannered, perfectly house-trained, and past the stage of chewing things or bouncing off the walls. I just want comfort, routine, and a family to love.

Because I am a dignified senior lady, I am looking for a peaceful, retirement-style home where I can truly be pampered as the queen of the couch.

My older joints aren’t as bouncy as they used to be, so a home with minimal or no major stairs (or a family willing to give me a little lift) would be absolutely perfect for me.

I would thrive best in a calm environment where I can soak up all the love, gentle attention, and cosy spot options I deserve.

I have so much gentle affection left to give, and I can’t wait to find my match. Could your home be my perfect retirement haven? Please get in touch to learn more about making me a part of your family!

Bonnie does have a condition called dry eye, so she will need regular drops to keep them lubricated, other than that, she is an absolute doll with the sweetest expression, surely someone out there has a space for this gorgeous old girl.

name: Mojo
description:
Mojo is an absolutely gorgeous little terrier mix that is approx. 8 years old. He was an unclaimed stray but we think he is a yorkie mix, he is only a dinky little fella, approx 4kg, and he was not microchipped.

On arrival we had him castrated, microchipped and he had a dental with quite a few teeth removed.

He has a lovely character that will melt you and he would make a fantastic companion for someone who likes the slower pace of life and a little buddy to talk to.

Mojo is a happy little guy that would love a family or person of his own, he absolutely loves food and snuggles – in no particular order!

Mojo is an inquisitive little guy, he likes to follow you around and has to know what’s going on, he is also a very laid back little lad perfect for an older person looking for a companion.

When Mojo first arrived he was pretty shell shocked, but as he has settled in his personality is shining through, he loves to run around with the other dogs in a secure field and he loves to sniff everything.

He has fab recall and walks lovely on a lead, he travels well and is an all round little pleasure to have.

He absolutely adores other dogs – especially the ladies, so could happily live with other dogs, that said he is also a very independent little man so would be happy as the only dog in the home as well.

Mojo is fine to be left for short periods and is a quiet little lad, not a barker like most smaller breeds. He will happily cuddle up in his bed, He is house trained however will scent mark in a new environment.

Mojo is a gorgeous happy little man that so desperately needs a forever home and family to grow up with. Mojo is neutered and recently had a dental, he is microchipped de flead and wormed.

name: Eto
description:
Eto is a two year old male Brittany. Eto is such a friendly, handsome young boy! Eto is a cheerful and lively dog, very energetic and active.

Eto is very affectionate and attached to people, loves cuddles and caresses, and obeys when called. He loves his food which will help with training.

Eto loves to run at full speed in the enclosure with his kennel mate Diana, with whom he has bonded from the first moment. He would love a doggy companion in his new home.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Eto a home, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue.

Eto is in Spain and ready to travel to his forever home in the UK.

name: Freya
description:
Freya is a 4 and a half year female Mastin cross located in Spain.

Pretty Freya is a big, beautiful girl, with a smooth, soft, black and white coat, Her facial markings are unique and just enhances her beauty.

Freya is a Mastin cross, she stands at medium size. She came to the rescue with her sister Eida who has since been adopted but poor Freya is still in the rescue waiting for her new family.

Initially she was very timid and scared of people, but she has much more confidence now and enjoys attention and fuss from the volunteers.

Freya is great with people and children, and very laid back and gentle, she is also a very sweet, pretty girl, just so friendly and loves a cuddle.

She is not a dominant female and therefore gets along with all dogs, during her time at the rescue she has shared with male and female dogs. She currently shares with Luke and they make a good pair together as he is more dominant. She is not cat tested.

She is at the perfect age to adapt into a new home and with some initial time to settle she will make a loyal, loving family pet.

She can live with other dogs and older children and Freya walks very well on her lead. The rescue where Freya is living is closing and so she is one of 35 dogs looking for a home quickly. Can you help Freya with a loving forever home?

Great with people and dogs. gentle nature, and is obedient, and a pretty girl.

name: Sky
description:
Sky is a four year old female English Setter. Beauiful Sky is currently in foster in Essex. Sky is a shy girl and needs a kind and patient home to help improve her confidence and bring her out of her shell.

Sky is currently living with other resident dogs and getting on well with them, although she can be nervous at first. Sky is nervous of people and will benefit from a friendly resident dog in a home long term to help show her the ropes.

She picks her own safe spaces in the home and is gradually learning to trustBACKGROUND

Sky was given to the shelter we work with in North Spain by her hunter who could no longer look after her. The poor girl arrived very nervous with a lot of insecurities, Being in a home will help her overcome her worries.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Sky a home, she is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Sky is currently in foster in Essex.

Can you offer Sky her forever home? Will that be with you?

name: Mac
description:
Mac, 3 years old, male, large cross breed.

Mac is a friendly boy who has waited a while in the shelter in Romania for the chance to travel to a new start in the Uk.

He is used to living with other dogs but has not been cat tested.

Mac would suit a family with older children, a couple or an individual who wants a soulmate of the dog kind!

He is gentle but due to his size her would probably be not suitable to live with young children.

He even has his own passport which holds all his medical records and procedures.

Mac has been fully vaccinated, including rabies and has had all the blood tests needed to comply with DEFRA regulations.

We deliver directly to the new adopter once checks have been done and we provide life long rescue back up.

name: Nero
description:
Nero is a 9-month-old male Cross-Breed. He is a large-sized dog with a playful and affectionate personality. His temperament is described as friendly and sociable, making him a great companion for a variety of households.

He is very cuddly and enjoys spending time with people. Nero is also good with other dogs and interacts well with them in social settings. His friendly nature extends to children, which means he could thrive in a family home.

However, Nero is not suitable to live with cats. This is an important factor for potential adopters to consider when thinking about their current household setup. Aside from this limitation, he appears adaptable and easy-going in most environments.

He will be rehomed with a full adoption package. This includes vaccinations, microchipping, blood testing, and neutering. These provisions ensure that he is well-prepared for his new home.

A full RBU is also included as part of the adoption process. A home check will be required to confirm that his new environment is suitable. These steps are important to ensure Nero’s long-term wellbeing.

Overall, Nero is a loving and energetic young dog with a friendly and gentle nature. He would suit an active household that can provide him with attention and companionship.

With the right home, he has the potential to become a loyal and devoted family member.

name: Zuri
description:
Zuri is a 9-month-old female Cross-Breed. She is described as a large-sized dog with a playful and affectionate nature. Her personality is friendly and sociable, making her a warm companion for people and families alike.

She is very cuddly and enjoys interaction, showing a gentle and loving temperament. Zuri gets along well with other dogs and thrives in their company. Her friendly behaviour also extends to children, making her suitable for a family environment.

However, she is not suitable to live with cats. This is an important consideration for households that already have feline companions. Aside from this, she appears adaptable and comfortable in social settings involving both humans and dogs.

Zuri is currently based in Cyprus but is able to travel to the UK or elsewhere in Europe. This makes her accessible to a wider range of adopters willing to arrange her relocation. Her transition would be supported with proper procedures already in place.

She will come with a full adoption package to ensure her health and wellbeing. This includes vaccinations, microchipping, blood testing, and neutering. These measures help provide reassurance that she is ready for a safe and healthy start in her new home.

A full RBU is also included as part of her adoption process. Additionally, a home check will be required to ensure that her new environment is suitable. These steps are in place to prioritise her long-term welfare and successful placement.

Overall, Zuri presents as a loving, energetic, and social dog who would do well in an active household. Her friendly disposition and compatibility with children and other dogs make her a strong candidate for many ???? types.

With the right home, she has the potential to become a loyal and affectionate companion.

name: Archie
description:
Archie is a lovely little tan and white male mixed breed who is currently in Oman. He is estimated to be born in December 2022 and was rescued off the streets of Oman as a young puppy.

He was taken in by a local rescuer where he stayed for approximately two years. Here he lived with many other dogs (large and small breed) and cats who he got along well with.

During this time, Archie suffered from skin mites which has sadly left him scarred.

Archie’s story is quite a sad one. Last year (2025), he had a home lined up in Germany but he sadly run off from his foster home and although we had search parties out day and night, we were unable to find him until 6 months later!

We aren’t sure how he managed to survive on the streets for all that time, we suspect someone may have taken him in, but when we were contacted about him, we immediately went to get him and brought him to the boarding facility where our other dogs reside.

Unfortunately, the adopters in Germany adopted another dog when they thought Archie was lost forever so he lost out on his forever home there.

Archie is a really lovely little dog. He is friendly especially once he knows you and loves playing with the other dogs in boarding. We think he would love a home with at least one other dog for company.

He could live alongside cats too. He could live with dog savvy/ respectful children.

We would love nothing more than to see him safe and loved in his forever home. We haven’t had any luck in finding this home in Oman so we are hoping his forever home is in the UK.

He is healthy, fully vaccinated, neutered and rabies titer tested so is ready to travel to the UK now. He will be tested for Brucella Canis before he leaves Oman.

name: Nellie
description:
Nellie is fostered in Spalding, Lincolnshire

Nellie was found abandoned as a 3 month old puppy in a small village in Romania, she was lucky and taken to a shelter until she was old enough to travel to the Uk.

Nellie is a bright, lively and inquisitive pup, she mixes well with other dogs but could also live as an only dog in a house where here person was at home most of the day.

Nellie is a little nervous when meeting new people but after receiving a couple of treats she is your friend for life.

Nellie would be happy living in a family environment with children 8 plus but she would be just as happy living with a couple or someone on their own, she would enjoy the attention.

Nellie is in foster home with other dogs so she is very familiar with living in a home and all the day to day activities that go on in a busy household, she is good on a lead, clean in the house and ok with being left for a few hours if she has the company of other dogs.

name: Lara
description:
Lara, this 5 year old female springer spaniel is the definition of a happy, active dog. She is the ultimate retriever — if you can throw it, she will chase it!

Balls, sticks, stones… even the occasional orange — she proudly collects her treasures and brings them back with pure excitement. She would thrive with an active person who enjoys walks, playtime, and a dog who’s always ready for the next adventure.

Despite her energy, Lara has an incredibly gentle soul. She is kind and calm with other animals and has a naturally sweet temperament that makes her easy to love.

Her past, however, was far from kind. Lara was found caged, severely underweight, and very unwell. But like many truly special dogs, she chose joy over fear. Today, she is full of life, energy, and affection — a true testament to her resilience.

Lara is also a Leishmania carrier, currently stable and well-managed with daily medication (Alopron 200, twice a day), which she takes without any fuss. She is regularly monitored and living a happy, healthy life.

She walks beautifully both on and off the lead, making her an easy and enjoyable companion outdoors.

While she gets along well with other animals, we believe Lara would truly flourish as the only dog in a home where she can receive all the love, attention, and activity she has been missing for so long.

Lara doesn’t just want a home — she’s ready to embrace life with someone who will truly be hers.

If you’re looking for a loyal, joyful, and energetic companion, Lara is waiting for you.

name: Reggie (Reginald)
description:
Reggie is a 5-year-old, neutered, microchipped and fully vaccinated spaniel boy who is ready to find his forever home.

This handsome guy is all heart. He absolutely lives for affection — hugs, attention, and being close to his person are what make him happiest. If you’re looking for a dog that will bond deeply and be by your side, Reggie is your dog.

He enjoys exploring and has excellent recall, happily roaming and always coming back to check in. He would thrive with an active owner who enjoys walks, outdoor time, and having a loyal companion along for the journey.

Reggie also has a natural protective instinct. He takes pride in watching over his home, often choosing to spend part of the evening outside keeping an eye on things before settling in for the night.

He’s the perfect mix of loving companion and gentle guardian.

While he gets along with other dogs and cats, we truly believe Reggie would flourish as the only pet in the home, where he can receive all the love and attention he craves.

Reggie is a healthy Leishmania carrier and is responsibly managed with daily medication (Alopron 200, twice a day), which he takes easily. He has been treated, is stable, and is regularly monitored.

His past wasn’t kind — he was found chained and already infected — but despite everything, he remains loving, trusting, and full of life. Now all he needs is someone to give him the safe, happy future he deserves.

Reggie isn’t just looking for a home — he’s looking for his person.

If you think you could be that person, he’s ready to meet you.

name: Kiri
description:
Kiri a is 2 year old male pointer mix. He was found by a friend of one of our volunteers who has cared for him in foster. It is now time to find him a loving forever home.

Kiri weights approximately 15kg he is medium size. He is neutered and fully vaccinated.

Kiri needs a fully secured private garden where he can run and play. He gets very excited when he meets you and does tend to jump up because he craves human attention.

It is something that can easily be overcome using positive reinforcement training techniques. Kiri is well socialised and gets along really well with other dogs.

Kiri is a typical pointer full of energy. His ideal home would be with an active family with a large secure garden.

He could be homed with another dog but would equally happy as an only dog with adopters who can commit to giving him time and patience and the exercise he needs.

Kiri will return this commitment with both unwavering love and loyalty.

name: Taco
description:
Taco is a one year old male mixed breed. Taco is a gorgeous young dog. He was handed to the shelter we work closely with because he is one of the many excess dogs no longer wanted in Spain.

When he arrived, he was quite scared, but with the companionship of the other dogs he quickly improved and overcame his fears.

Taco is very affectionate with people and charming. He loves being in the enclosure running and playing with his companion. He shares a kennel with a female dog, he loves to play with her and other dogs

If you are interested in giving wonderful Taco a home, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Taco is in Spain and ready to travel to his forever home in the UK.

name: Zeus
description:
Meet our dear Zeus – a truly wonderful boy looking for his forever home.

Originally rescued from Croatia, Zeus is now ready to start his next chapter with an active, loving family.

If you enjoy the great outdoors, Zeus will be your perfect walking companion. He absolutely thrives in nature and walks beautifully alongside a pack of dogs. Exploring woodland trails, countryside paths, or long weekend adventures would be his dream come true.

Zeus is happiest when he’s out and about, taking in the sights and smells of the world around him. With his warm presence and love for adventure, he’ll make a loyal and devoted companion for someone who enjoys an active lifestyle.

Zeus loves his people and wants to be close to them most of the time

He forms strong bonds and enjoys being part of the family. When he’s not out exploring, he’s more than happy to snuggle up on the sofa and enjoy some well-earned cuddle time.

Zeus is a rescue dog who already has great potential. With his love of the outdoors, beautiful pack walking skills, and affectionate nature, he’s just waiting for the right home to truly shine.

Let’s get our gorgeous boy into a loving home.

He made such a long journey and now he’s stuck in kennels through no fault of his own

Could you be the one to give Zeus the forever home he deserves?

name: Cindy
description:
Cindy, our 1 year old disabled female mixed breed was allowed to roam freely as a puppy by her family in Cyprus — until one tragic day in October last year, she was hit by a car.

When they learned she would need an expensive surgery to survive, her family walked away, leaving her behind. They said they no longer wanted her… and left her in pain.

Fast forward to now: Cindy, we know, will remain paralysed in her back legs, she has been receiving regular laser treatment which has massively helped her, and she loves life with her foster mum and all the other dogs.

But it’s time for little Cindy to belong and have her own forever family, she is still a baby, 15 months old and just 6 kilos.

We will cover her flight costs if she is adopted in the UK. We are not looking for a foster home as she already is in a wonderful foster home. We are looking for an extra special forever family.

Despite her disability Cindy is full of life, happy and playful girl.

She can take some time to warm up to people who she hasn’t met before, the same with other dogs. But once she knows she is safe, she is very sweet and loves attention.

She gets around the house just fine without her wheels, she can also get into dog beds with no issues, steps are still a work in progress, and she will sit and cry if she gets “stuck” and unable to come back up them.

Cindy loves time in her wheels in open spaces where she can run and explore, she is amazingly quick in them, even out of them she’s quick too.

Cindy is understandably afraid of cars, we have been working on building her confidence with them, and she has since walked (in her wheels) down a side walk with a few cars passing, but if something bigger or louder was to pass she will freeze and then not want to walk any more.

She can poop and pee by herself, but it’s best to check if her bladder is empty 2-3 times a day just to prevent the chances of a urinary infection.

Cindy is currently on a RAW diet, as this keeps her poo firm (easy to clean up) and keeps her regular. Her two favourite times of day are breakfast and dinner, she is a little foody!

Are you the person we are looking for, that special person who can look beyond Cindy’s disability and who can see that in every other way Cindy is just an adorable pooch looking for a chance to live her best life.

name: Wilson
description:
Wilson is a 2 year old male Hound Cross. He was rescued in Cyprus as a baby of six months and flew to his current home in Mold, Wales at around a year old. He weighs around 27 kg.

Wilson is a deeply affectionate dog who forms strong bonds once he feels safe. When he trusts you, he is a total sofa snuggler and would happily spend the day curled up beside you, soaking up all the love.

Indoors, he is calm, settled, and content to relax, making him a lovely presence in the home.

Outside, Wilson has a playful side and enjoys stretching his legs in open spaces. He absolutely loves chasing his frisbee, although returning it is not really his strong point. He is more about the joy of the chase than the fetch itself.

Wilson walks beautifully on the lead when it is quiet. He can become excited and reactive when he sees other dogs, particularly at the start of a walk, but with calm handling and distraction he does settle.

Off lead, he enjoys playing with other dogs, although he can get a bit over-excited and benefits from gentle time-outs to help him calm himself.

He is excellent around food, with no begging, stealing, or guarding, and is fully house trained, crate trained, and sleeps soundly through the night. He can be left for a few hours without distress and does not suffer from separation anxiety.

Wilson is brilliant with familiar people and has been lovely with the children in his current home. However, he is a sensitive and easily spooked boy.

For this reason, he would be best suited to a quieter, adult-only home with minimal unexpected noise or activity, where he can truly relax and feel secure.

Wilson is being rehomed through no fault of his own. Sadly, despite time and patience, he has not been able to feel safe around one member of his current household and is living in a constant state of anxiety.

His family love him dearly and want him to have the calm, peaceful life he deserves.

Wilson would thrive in a calm, adult-only home with experienced or understanding adopters, a quiet environment with predictable routines, and someone willing to let him build trust at his own pace.

In the right home, Wilson will be an incredibly loyal and loving companion who gives his whole heart to his person. If you are looking for a gentle soul to share quiet days, cosy evenings, and meaningful bonds, Wilson could be your perfect match.

If you think you could be Wilson’s person, please get in touch.

Where in the country you liveYour experience with dogsA brief description of your garden and height of fencing at its lowest pointDetails of other dog or dogs in your homeAny other petsAges of any children in your home or who may visitTime a dog might be left alone each day and how they will fit into your lifestyleYour best contact number

He has been vaccinated, neutered, and microchipped.

A minimum adoption donation of £300 applies.

Adoption is subject to a satisfactory application and home check.

Post-adoption support is available from the rescue.

The rescue must be informed at any time of a change in circumstances. Wilson must never be handed over to any UK rescue or sold or adopted on without their knowledge. They will always endeavour to rehome their dogs when necessary.

name: Lily
description:
Lily is a 2 year old female Labrador Retriever Cross. She is a beautiful young mixed-breed girl with a look that hints at Labrador heritage and a personality full of life and love.

Rescued from Cyprus, she is now based near Peacehaven and ready to find her perfect forever home.

At nearly two years old, Lily is in her prime—full of energy, curiosity, and affection. She weighs around 22 kg and stands approximately 60 cm at the shoulder.

She thrives on playtime, especially chasing a ball or enjoying a good tug toy session, and she is just as happy settling down afterward for a well-earned rest.

Lily is house-trained, clean, and sleeps soundly through the night in her crate for up to nine hours. She sees her crate as her safe space and settles well after walks, though she does enjoy having people around when she is awake.

She communicates clearly too—expect a loud bark when she needs to go outside.

Out on walks, Lily is generally good on the lead, though she can get excited and pull if something catches her eye—especially squirrels or rabbits, as she has a strong prey drive.

Her recall is improving well, and she responds reliably to a whistle when using a long line.

She is friendly and sociable with other dogs when out and about, often engaging in playful, appropriate interactions, particularly with younger, energetic dogs.

However, due to her high energy and enthusiasm, she would be best suited as the only dog in the home or with a similarly playful companion. She would not be suitable for a home with cats or small animals.

Lily has not yet been fully assessed around children, as she is still quite bouncy and can jump up or mouth when excited. Therefore, any children in her new home should be older and confident around dogs. With continued training and guidance, she is making great progress and shows every sign of becoming a wonderfully well-rounded dog.

The only reason Lily is looking for a new home is due to a mismatch with the resident older dog, who cannot meet her playful needs. This has led to a few incidents driven by Lily’s excitement rather than aggression.

Lily is a truly sweet and affectionate girl who is learning quickly and eager to please. In the right home—one that can match her energy, continue her training, and give her the love and structure she needs—she will make an incredibly loyal and loving companion.

Please, when contacting, share the following:

Where you liveYour experience with dogsYour garden and fencing (height at lowest point)Other pets in the homeAges of children in the home or who visitHow long Lily may be left alone and how she will fit into your lifestyleYour best contact number

Lily is neutered, vaccinated, and microchipped. A minimum adoption donation of £300 applies. Adoption is subject to a satisfactory application and home check.

The rescue is committed to the lifelong care of their dogs and will always accept their return when space allows. In situations where space is limited, they will endeavour to rehome the dog directly from its current home.

Under no circumstances may the dog be transferred to another UK rescue organisation.

name: Bonnie
description:
Bonnie, also known as Bonbon, is an approximately 3 year old spayed female large mixed breed currently in foster care in Doncaster.

Bonnie is a gentle and sensitive dog who can be shy when meeting new people. She prefers a calm environment and takes time to build trust. Once bonded, she is affectionate and enjoys close companionship.

She is not aggressive but can be nervous around unfamiliar visitors. A quiet household with limited visitors will help her feel secure. She benefits from patient handling and consistent routine.

Bonnie thrives in the company of other dogs and must live with a calm, confident resident dog for reassurance and companionship.

She has previously lived with cats and may attempt to initiate play, so slow and managed introductions are required.

She is housetrained and crate trained. She sleeps overnight in her crate and can be left alone for short periods.

Bonnie walks well on a lead in quieter areas but remains cautious in busier environments. She is currently exercised on a long line due to a flight risk, and a secure garden is essential.

Continued confidence-building and structured training will be important.

Bonnie enjoys gentle play, grooming and relaxed time with her people. She responds well to food-based training.

Bonnie would suit a calm, rural or low-traffic home with patient adopters experienced in handling shy or sensitive dogs. Adults or older children who understand her need for space would be most appropriate.

name: Lupin
description:
Meet Lupin, a 4 month old male Griffon Cross who is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog of around 18–20 kg when fully grown.

Lupin is a charming young puppy born on 1 November 2025. He is one of six brothers born to a Griffon cross mum.

Lupin has spent his early months at the Residencia Garatuxa shelter in Galicia, where he has grown up surrounded by people, other dogs, and everyday shelter activity. This has helped him develop into a sociable and confident puppy.

He enjoys playing with his brothers and interacting with people, showing a friendly and open nature. Lupin will thrive in a home where he can continue learning, exploring, and becoming a much-loved family member.

He has been tested for Mediterranean diseases and will be fully prepared for travel, vaccinated, microchipped, and with his passport ready. Lupin will be ready to travel in April.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Hamish
description:
Meet Hamish, a 4 month old male Griffon Cross who is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog of around 18–20 kg when fully grown.

Hamish is one of six lively brothers born on 1 November 2025 to a Griffon cross mum. He is currently nearly four months old and, like his siblings, is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog.

Hamish has had a good start to life at the Residencia Garatuxa shelter in Galicia, northern Spain. Growing up in the shelter environment means he is already used to people, everyday activity, and different sounds around him.

He is a very sociable puppy who enjoys interacting with both humans and other dogs.

As a young puppy, Hamish will benefit from a family willing to continue his training and give him the guidance, exercise, and affection he needs as he grows.

He has been tested for Mediterranean diseases and will be fully prepared for travel, vaccinated, microchipped, and with his passport ready. Hamish will be ready to travel in April to the right home.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Jester
description:
Introducing Jester, a 4 month old male Griffon Cross who is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog of around 18–20 kg.

Jester was born on 1 November 2025 as part of a litter of six boys. His mother is a Griffon cross, and he and his brothers have been raised at the Residencia Garatuxa shelter in Galicia.

During their time at the shelter, they have had regular contact with people and other dogs. This has helped them grow into confident, sociable puppies who are comfortable around activity and noise.

Jester is affectionate, playful, and curious about the world around him. Like all puppies, he will need a family ready to guide him through training and provide the love and stability every young dog deserves.

He has been tested for Mediterranean diseases and will be fully prepared for travel, vaccinated, microchipped, and with his passport ready. Jester will be ready to travel in April to his forever home.

As with all of our dogs, he comes with full rescue back-up.

name: Pongo
description:
Pongo is a 1-year-old male Labrador Retriever Cross. He currently weighs around 25 kg and is described as a sweet and gentle dog with a sociable nature.

Although he may appear a little shy when first meeting new people, he gradually becomes more confident once he feels safe and comfortable.

Pongo’s early life began in Italy, where he was found as a very young puppy. When he was around two months old, he and his small siblings, along with other puppies, were captured and taken to a shelter.

Life behind the bars of a shelter was not the start any young dog deserves, but fortunately his story soon took a more hopeful turn.

A kind woman in Germany decided to rescue him and offer him a chance at a better life. Thanks to her, Pongo was able to leave the shelter and move into a foster home in Germany. There he is now patiently waiting for the loving family he truly deserves.
